LFS and BLFS Security Advisories from September 2020 onwards

LFS has not reported Security Vulnerabilities in the Errata, at least recently, but tickets for some new versions have had details.

BLFS used to keep details of Security Vulnerabilities in the Errata, mostly updating them to point to the latest version in the development book and updating the brief text if a subsequent vulnerability was reported.

This page is a consolidated list for both LFS and BLFS.

This list contains summary details and links to upstreams or CVEs where available. Please note that vulnerabilities to package versions before those in our 10.0 releases are not noted, so if you are running a version of BLFS before 10.0 you should check the Errata for past releases as well as monitoring the items here.

This page is ordered like the Changelog of the books, with newest items first.

The severity ratings are best estimates unless either upstream or NVD has assigned a rating. If no other analysis is available, High will usually be assumed and similarly if a crash can be triggered LFS and BLFS will normally rate that as High. If in doubt, read the links.

Items between the releases of the 12.4 and 13.0 books

12.4 093 PostgreSQL Date: 2026-02-14 Severity: High

In PostgreSQL-18.2, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for memory disclosure, arbitrary code execution, and privilege escalation. The first issue (which causes memory disclosure) is caused by improper validation of oidvector, and it allows for database users to disclose a few bytes of server memory. The next issue allows for arbitrary code execution due to missing validation of types of input in the intarray extension selectivity function, which allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the user running the database. The next issue is a heap buffer overflow in pgcrypto, which allows a ciphertext provider to execute arbitrary code as the user running the database. The next issue is caused by missing validation of multibyte character length when performing text manipulation, allowing database users to issue crafted queries that achieve a buffer overrun and then executes arbitrary code as the user running the database. The final issue is a possible privilege escalation issue caused by a heap buffer overflow in pg_trgm, which allows a database user to write a pattern onto server memory. All users who have PostgreSQL setup as a database server should update immediately, but the client libraries seem to be unaffected. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-2003, CVE-2026-2004, CVE-2026-2005, CVE-2026-2006, and CVE-2026-2007.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to PostgreSQL-18.2 using the instructions from PostgreSQL (sysv) or PostgreSQL (systemd). If you are on PostgreSQL-17 and don't want to update your database to 18.x, update to PostgreSQL-17.8 instead using the instructions from PostgreSQL (12.4 sysv) or PostgreSQL (12.4 systemd).

12.4 092 intel-microcode Date: 2026-02-11 Severity: High

In intel-microcode-20260210, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for privilege escalation or for a denial of service (application crash). The first privilege escalation vulnerability affects all Intel Core CPUs from the 6th generation to the 11th generation of CPUs, as well as some CPUs from the Intel Pentium Gold and Celeron families. Some CPUs from the Xeon W, E, D, and the 2nd/3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable CPU family are also impacted. The other privilege escalation vulnerability affects 10th generation Intel Core CPUs and later, including the Core Ultra processor family, and some Intel Pentium and Celeron CPUs are affected. In addition, the 3rd generation and later of Intel Xeon Scalable Processors are affected, as well as some Xeon E, W, and D series processors. Several functionality issues with the 10th generation and later of Intel Core CPUs have been resolved, including the Core i3 N-series and several Xeon CPU families. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-24853 and CVE-2025-31648.

Additional information about these vulnerabilities can be found at the Intel Security Advisories:

  • INTEL-SA-01083 (CVE-2024-24853)
  • INTEL-SA-01396 (CVE-2025-31648)

Check if your CPU is affected by running lscpu and comparing the outputted family, model, and stepping values with the values provided above and in INTEL-SA-01083 and INTEL-SA-01396, If your system is vulnerable, update to intel-microcode-20260210 or later using the instructions from About Firmware (sysv) or About Firmware (systemd).

12.4 091 libjxl Date: 2026-02-11 Severity: High

In libjxl-0.11.2, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash), information disclosure, or remote code execution. The first vulnerability occurs because a specially crafted file can cause libjxl's decoder to read pixel data from uninitialized memory by referencing an outside image bound area in a subsequent path. This is caused by an incorrect optimization which causes the decoder to omit populating these areas. The other vulnerability affects BLFS installations in particular because BLFS uses lcms2 for the color management backend. The vulnerability allows for significant remote code execution and information disclosure impacts when a specially crafted file is loaded into libjxl's decoder that requests a color transformation of grayscale images to another grayscale color space. Users who have libjxl installed should update to this version immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-12474 and CVE-2026-1837.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libjxl-0.11.2 or later using the instructions from libjxl (sysv) or libjxl (systemd).

12.4 090 libpng Date: 2026-02-11 Severity: High

In libpng-1.6.55, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for information disclosure, remote code execution, and denial of service (application crashes). The vulnerability occurs in valid PNG files, and occurs in the png_set_quantize function. The issue is a heap buffer overflow, and can be exploited in any context where a system may load a PNG image. Unlike the more recent libpng security updates, this affects the low level functions that many more applications use. Users who have libpng installed for any reason should update immediately. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2026-25646.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libpng-1.6.55 or later using the instructions from libpng (sysv) or libpng (systemd).

12.4 089 GnuTLS Date: 2026-02-11 Severity: High

In GnuTLS-3.8.12, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash or resource exhaustion). The first vulnerability is a NULL pointer dereference during PSK binder verification. This can occur when a TLS 1.3 resumption attempt with an invalid PSK binder value in ClientHello is received and processed. Upstream resolved the issue by adding additional code guards against the problematic dereference. The other vulnerability occurs when verifying certificates with pathological amounts of name constraints, as a performance issue was found when processing excessive amounts of them. Upstream reworked the processing algorithms to prevent resource exhaustion from occuring. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-1584 and CVE-2025-14831.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to GnuTLS-3.8.12 or later using the instructions from GnuTLS (sysv) or GnuTLS (systemd).

12.4 088 Python (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2026-08-08 Severity: High

In Python-3.11.12 and Python-3.14.2, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for header injection within Python's WSGI support whenever wsgiref.headers.Headers fields, values, and parameters are supplied a C0 control character, for header injection to occur whenever the http.cookie.Morsel function is used with a control character within the cookie parameters, for header injection whenever newlines are supplied in data: URL media types, for header injection when flattening an email message using a modern email policy, and for header injection when using the BytesGenerator class from the "email" module. Note that these vulnerabilities primarily affect web server and email contexts, so users not using that functionality are not affected by these vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-0865, CVE-2026-1299, CVE-2026-0672, CVE-2025-15282, and CVE-2025-11468.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update Python. If you are on Python-3.13.x, update to Python-3.13.12. Meanwhile, if you are on Python-3.14.x, update to Python-3.14.3. In order to do so, follow the instructions from Python (sysv) or Python (systemd).

12.4 087 p11-kit Date: 2026-02-08 Severity: High

In p11-kit-0.26.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a remotely exploitable denial of service. The vulnerability is in the C_DeriveKey function, and occurs when using specific NULL parameters. These parameters can be set when processing a remote token with specific IBM kyber or IBM btc derive mechanism parameters. While the issue only allows for a remotely exploitable denial of service, upstream has rated it as High because the attack complexity is low. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2026-2100..

To fix this vulnerability, update to p11-kit-0.26.2 or later using the instructions from p11-kit (sysv) or p11-kit (systemd).

12.4 086 Expat (LFS) Date: 2026-02-08 Severity: Medium

In Expat-2.7.4, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash) or for remote code execution. The first vulnerability is in the XML_ExternalEntityParserCreate function, and it occurs because the function fails to copy the encoding handler data passed to XML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler from the parent to it's new parser. This causes a NULL pointer dereference from external entities that declare use of an unknown encoding. Note that an application must use both the XML_ExternalEntityParserCreate and XML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler functions to be vulnerable. The other vulnerability is in the doContent function, and occurs because the function does not properly determine the buffer size to use because there is no integer overflow check for tag buffer reallocation. This could result in a remote code execution problem depending on whether the application in use accepts untrusted input. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-24515 and CVE-2026-25210.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Expat-2.7.4 or later using the instructions from the LFS book for Expat (sysv) or Expat (systemd).

Note: If you have installed docbook-utils from BLFS you will need to add "--without-docbook" to work around an error in configure, since our installation of docbook-utils uses SGML instead of XML.

12.4 085 Qt6 Date: 2026-02-05 Severity: Critical

In Qt6-6.10.2 and QtWebEngine-6.10.2, 14 security vulnerabilities were resolved that could allow for remote code execution, remote arbitrary file read/writes, mark of the web bypasses, sensitive information exfiltration via remote access of the network log file, and denial of service (application crashes). One of these issues is in the QtDeclarative component within Qt itself, while the other 13 are in QtWebEngine. The QtWebEngine issues are vulnerabilities fixed in the bundled copy of Chromium, affecting it's ANGLE, V8, WebRTC, Loader, Media Stream, Downloads, and Network components. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-14576, CVE-2025-13042, CVE-2025-14174, CVE-2025-13639, CVE-2025-13638, CVE-2025-13721, CVE-2025-13720, CVE-2025-13634, CVE-2025-13224, CVE-2025-141765, CVE-2026-0899, CVE-2026-0905, CVE-2026-0908, and CVE-2026-1220.

Users are advised to resolve these vulnerabilities immediately by updating to Qt6-6.10.2 and QtWebEngine-6.10.2 or later, using the instructions from Qt6 (sysv) or Qt6 (systemd) and QtWebEngine (sysv) or QtWebEngine (systemd).

12.4 084 FreeRDP Date: 2026-02-05 Severity: High

In FreeRDP-3.22.0, a grand total of 12 security vulnerabilities were fixed that are in the FreeRDP client itself. One of the issues can also affect the FreeRDP proxy handling code. Information on these vulnerabilities isn't available yet other than the CVE numbers, as GitHub advisories have not been issued for this release yet. Users should update FreeRDP however due to the amount of issues resolved. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-23948, CVE-2026-24682, CVE-2026-24683, CVE-2026-24676, CVE-2026-24677, CVE-2026-24678, CVE-2026-24684, CVE-2026-24679, CVE-2026-24681, CVE-2026-24675, CVE-2026-24491, and CVE-2026-24680.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to FreeRDP-3.22.0 or later using the instructions from FreeRDP (sysv) or FreeRDP (systemd).

12.4 083 GnuPG Date: 2026-02-05 Severity: High

In GnuPG-2.5.17, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution and denial of service (application crashes) when processing GnuPG data. The first vulnerability occurs because a crafted CMS (S/MIME) EncryptedData message carrying an oversized wrapped session key can cause a stack buffer overflow in the gpg-agent utility when it performs PKDECRYPT--kem=CMS handling. This results in memory corruption that is known to lead to remote code execution. The second vulnerability occurs in the internal tpm2daemon when handling the PKDECRYPT command for TPM-backed RSA and ECC keys. This issue is another stack buffer overflow that allows for remote code execution. The third vulnerability is in the parse_signature function, where a long signature packet length causes that function to return success with it's data values set to NULL, leading to an application crash. Users who have GnuPG installed are urged to update to this version of GnuPG. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-24881, CVE-2026-24882, and CVE-2026-24883.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to GnuPG-2.5.17 or later using the instructions from GnuPG (sysv) or GnuPG (systemd).

12.4 082 BIND Date: 2026-02-05 Severity: High

In BIND-9.20.18, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for remote attackers to force the BIND DNS server to terminate unexpectedly. The problem occurs whenever the server receives and attempts to parse malformed BRID or HHIT records. The maximum extent of the vulnerability is a denial of service condition (crash), but because it can be exploited via standard DNS resolution, so users who are using it for a local caching resolver can also be impacted by this vulnerability. However, the client utilities are not impacted. If you are using BIND as a DNS server in any capacity though, the BLFS team recommends updating to this version. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-13878.

To fix this vulnerability, update to BIND-9.20.18 or later using the instructions from BIND (sysv) or BIND (systemd).

12.4 081 Thunderbird Date: 2026-02-04 Severity: Medium

In Thunderbird-140.7.1esr, one security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for modification or transfer of data from CSS in a partially encrypted email once remote content is allowed. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2026-0818.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Thunderbird-140.7.1esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.4 080 gst-plugins-bad Date: 2026-02-04 Severity: High

In gst-plugins-bad-1.26.10, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for out-of-bounds read operations in the MIDI parser, in turn leading to a crash (DOS). Not many packages in BLFS, if any, use the MIDI parser from gst-plugins-bad. Most opt for other solutions like FluidSynth. There is still a possibility of a package using it, so users should update regardless. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-67326 and CVE-2025-67327.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to gstreamer, gst-plugins-base, and gst-plugins-bad 1.26.10 or later using the instructions from gstreamer (sysv) or gstreamer (systemd), gst-plugins-base (sysv) or gst-plugins-base (systemd), and gst-plugins-bad (sysv) or gst-plugins-bad (systemd).

gstreamer-1.28.0 is ABI compatible with 1.26.x.

12.4 079 glibc (LFS) Date: 2026-02-01 Severity: High

In glibc-2.43, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for buffer overflows, failure to save and restore nonvolatile vectors, and double-free operations. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-0395, CVE-2025-5702, CVE-2025-5745, and CVE-2025-8058.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to glibc-2.43 using the instructions from the LFS book for glibc (sysv) or glibc (systemd).

12.4 078 OpenSSL (LFS) Date: 2026-02-01 Severity: High

In OpenSSL-3.6.1, twelve security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for denial of service (DOS) attacks, stack buffer overflows, NULL dereferencing operations, input truncation, excessive memory allocation, out-of-bounds write operations, trailing bytes, missing validation for ASN1, NULL pointer dereferencing operations, and type confusion. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-11187, CVE-2025-15467, CVE-2025-15468, CVE-2025-15469, CVE-2025-66199, CVE-2025-68160, CVE-2025-69418, CVE-2025-69419, CVE-2025-69420, CVE-2025-69421, CVE-2026-22795, and CVE-2026-22796.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to OpenSSL-3.6.1 (or 3.5.5) using the instructions from the LFS book for OpenSSL (sysv) or OpenSSL (systemd).

12.4 077 FreeRDP Date: 2026-01-21 Severity: High

In FreeRDP-3.21.0, eight security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for heap buffer overflows, global buffer overflows, and use-after-free operations which can cause a crash (DOS) and heap corruption. All of these vulnerabilities occur client-side. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-23530, CVE-2026-23531, CVE-2026-23532, CVE-2026-23533, CVE-2026-23534, CVE-2026-23732, CVE-2026-23883, and CVE-2026-23884.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to FreeRDP-3.21.0 or later using the instructions from FreeRDP (sysv) or FreeRDP (systemd).

12.4 076 libpng Date: 2026-01-14 Severity: Medium

In libpng-1.6.54, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for heap buffer over-read operations. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2026-22695 and CVE-2026-22801.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libpng-1.6.54 or later using the instructions from libpng (sysv) or libpng (systemd).

12.4 075 Seamonkey Date: 2026-01-14 Severity: High

In Seamonkey-2.53.23, nineteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for race conditions, mitigation bypassing, use-after-free operations, spoofing, incorrect boundary conditions, same-origin policy bypassing, sandbox escapes, privilege escalations, JIT miscompilations, and memory safety expoitation. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-13012, CVE-2025-13013, CVE-2025-13014, CVE-2025-13015, CVE-2025-13016, CVE-2025-13017, CVE-2025-13018, CVE-2025-13019, CVE-2025-13020, CVE-2025-13021, CVE-2025-13022, CVE-2025-13023, CVE-2025-13024, CVE-2025-13025, CVE-2025-13028, CVE-2025-13029, CVE-2025-14330, CVE-2025-14331, and CVE-2025-14333.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Seamonkey-2.53.23 or later using the instructions from Seamonkey (sysv) or Seamonkey (systemd).

12.4 074 Thunderbird Date: 2026-01-14 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-140.7.0esr, thirteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for spoofing, mitigation bypassing, sandbox escapes, use-after-free operations, information disclosure, incorrect boundary conditions, clickjacking, and memory safety exploitation. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-14327, CVE-2026-0877, CVE-2026-0878, CVE-2026-0879, CVE-2026-0880, CVE-2026-0882, CVE-2026-0883, CVE-2026-0884, CVE-2026-0885, CVE-2026-0886, CVE-2026-0887, CVE-2026-0890, and CVE-2026-0891.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-140.7.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.4 073 SpiderMonkey Date: 2025-12-16 Severity: High

In SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.7.0esr, five security vulnerabilities were fixed fixed that could allow for sandbox escapes and use-after-free operations. These vulnerabilities has been assigned CVE-2026-0878, CVE-2026-0879, CVE-2026-0880, CVE-2026-0884, and CVE-2026-0885.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.7.0esr using the instructions from SpiderMonkey (sysv) or SpiderMonkey (systemd).

12.4 072 Firefox Date: 2026-01-14 Severity: High

In Firefox-140.7.0esr, thirteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for spoofing, mitigation bypassing, sandbox escapes, use-after-free operations, information disclosure, incorrect boundary conditions, clickjacking, and memory safety exploitation. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-14327, CVE-2026-0877, CVE-2026-0878, CVE-2026-0879, CVE-2026-0880, CVE-2026-0882, CVE-2026-0883, CVE-2026-0884, CVE-2026-0885, CVE-2026-0886, CVE-2026-0887, CVE-2026-0890, and CVE-2026-0891.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-140.7.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd). Do note that if you want to use NSS and NSPR for Firefox, NSPR must be at version 4.38.2.

12.4 071 Node.js Date: 2026-01-14 Severity: High

In Node.js-22.22.0, six security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for permission model bypassing, file system permission bypassing, timeout-based race conditions, read-only permission model bypassing, HTTP/2 server crashes, and process crashes. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-55130, CVE-2025-55131, CVE-2025-55132, CVE-2025-59465, CVE-2025-59466, and CVE-2026-21637.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Node.js-22.22.0 or later using the instructions from Node.js (sysv) or Node.js (systemd).

12.4 070 VLC Date: 2026-01-14 Severity: Critical

In VLC-3.0.23, twenty-two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for out-of-bounds reads and writes, invalid memory freeing operations, stack overflows, integer overflows, NULL dereferences, undefined shifting, infinite loops, buffer overflows, and multiple-format overflows. Only one of these vulnerabilities have had a CVE assigned, and it's for an out-of-bounds read operation. It has been assigned CVE-2025-51602.

Since there are so many vulnerabilties fixed, it is highly recommended to update immediately to VLC-3.0.23 or later by using the instructions from VLC (sysv) or VLC (systemd).

12.4 069 libtasn1 Date: 2026-01-14 Severity: High

In libtasn1-4.21.0, one security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a stack buffer overflow. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-13151.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libtasn1-4.21.0 or later using the instructions from libtasn1 (sysv) or libtasn1 (systemd).

12.4 068 cURL Date: 2026-01-14 Severity: Medium

In cURL-8.18.0, six security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for lack of QUIC certificate pinning with GnuTLS, broken TLS options, bearer token leakage, OpenSSL partial chain store policy bypassing, libssh global known_hosts overriding, and libssh key passphrase bypassing. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-13034, CVE-2025-14017, CVE-2025-14524, CVE-2025-14819, CVE-2025-15079, and CVE-2025-15224.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to cURL-8.18.0 or later using the instructions from cURL (sysv) or cURL (systemd).

12.4 067 OpenJDK Date: 2026-01-07 Severity: High

In OpenJDK-21.0.9, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for unauthenticated attackers to access any data on a system running a Java application, for an unauthenticated attacker to create, modify, or delete data accessible to a Java application, and for remotely exploitable crashes. The data access vulnerability is under active exploitation, and evidence has been shown that it's easy to exploit. The vulnerabilities are in the JAXP, Security, and Libraries components. None of the vulnerabilities require any user interaction or authentication to exploit. BLFS 12.4 shipped with Java 24.0.2, but it's highly recommended that users downgrade to 21.0.9 as it is the current LTS that works with the applications in BLFS. Java 25 causes problems with Apache ANT, fop, and others, and the BLFS team has elected to downgrade to the 21.x series instead. No changes are required to other packages in the book to use this version of Java. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-53066, CVE-2025-53057, and CVE-2025-61748.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to OpenJDK-21.0.9 or later using the instructions from OpenJDK (sysv) or OpenJDK (systemd).

If you want to use the pre-built binaries, update to Java-21.0.9 using the instructions from Java (sysv) or Java (systemd).

12.4 066 libpcap Date: 2025-12-31 Severity: Low

In libpcap-1.10.6, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash) when applications call the pcap_ether_aton() function with crafted inputs. The function takes in a string argument and returns a fixed-size allocated buffer, but the string argument must be a well-formed MAC-48 address in a supported format, and the requirement was not documented well. If an application calls the function with an argument that deviates from the expected format, the function can read data beyond the end of the provided string and write data beyond the end of the buffer that gets allocated. In the case of BLFS however, the only applications that use libpcap are Wireshark, nmap, and umockdev. If you notice crashes in these applications, you should update to this version of libpcap. However, upstream has rated the vulnerability as Low because the attack complexity is high and it requires root privileges to exploit. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-11961.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libpcap-1.10.6 or later using the instructions from libpcap (sysv) or libpcap (systemd).

12.4 065 Ruby Date: 2025-12-31 Severity: Low

In Ruby-3.4.8, a security vulnerability was fixed in the bundled REXML gem that can allow for a denial of service condition (application crash). The vulnerability can occur when parsing XML that has multiple XML declarations, but users are unaffected unless they are processing untrusted XML files through Ruby. If you process untrusted XML files and notice crashes, you should update to this version of Ruby. Otherwise though there is no need to upgrade. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-58767.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Ruby-3.4.8 or later using the instructions from Ruby (sysv) or Ruby (systemd).

12.4 064 PHP Date: 2025-12-28 Severity: Medium

In PHP-8.5.1, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for information disclosure, heap buffer overflows, and denial of service conditions (resource exhaustion and crashes). One of these vulnerabilities occurs in a common component bundled with PHP that is also used by other packages not in BLFS, known as uriparser. The remainder of the issues occur in the PDO, Standard Library, and URI components. Users who have PHP installed for any reason are recommended to update to this version of PHP because of the vulnerabilities in the Standard Library. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-14177, CVE-2025-14178, CVE-2025-14180, and CVE-2025-67899.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to PHP-8.5.1 or later using the instructions from PHP (sysv) or PHP (systemd).

Alternatively, users may use PHP-8.4.16 using the same instructions.

12.4 063 Python (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-12-23 Severity: Medium

In Python-3.13.11 and Python-3.14.2, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for accepting inconsistent zip64 central directory records, incorrect handling of maximum rows, lack of support for the plaintext element, unensured linear complexity for parsing legacy HTTP parameters, incorrect quadratic complexity, and denial of services. Some of these vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-8291, CVE-2025-12084, CVE-2025-13836, and CVE-2025-13837. The rest haven't been assigned CVEs but have GitHub issues associated with them: gh-136063, gh-137836, and gh-139283.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update Python. If you are on Python-3.13.x, update to Python-3.13.11. Meanwhile, if you are on Python-3.14.x, update to Python-3.14.2. In order to do so, follow the instructions from Python (sysv) or Python (systemd).

12.4 062 Exim Date: 2025-12-20 Severity: High

In Exim-4.99.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a remote heap buffer overflow in some situations because database records are cast directly to internal structures without validation. This only affects some non-default rate-limit configurations when using SQLite or hintdb as the database backend. The default configuration in BLFS is not affected, but if you have modified the rate limit configurations, you should update to Exim-4.99.1. There is no need to update otherwise. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-67896.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Exim-4.99.1 or later using the instructions from Exim (sysv) or Exim (systemd).

12.4 061 Kea DHCP Server Date: 2025-12-20 Severity: High

In Kea-3.0.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for clients to crash the DHCP server. This issue is highly configuration dependent. Unfortunately though, the default BLFS configuration is affected because it uses Dynamic DNS updates. Users who are using the default BLFS configuration of Kea should update to 3.0.2 as soon as possible because the vulnerability is easy to exploit with certain options contained in DHCP requests. For users not using the BLFS configuration, you are affected if "hostname-char-replacement" is empty (which is the default setting), "hostname-char-set" is at the default setting, and "ddns-qualifying-suffix" is NOT empty. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-11232.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Kea-3.0.2 or later using the instructions from Kea (sysv) or Kea (systemd).

12.4 060 WebKitGTK Date: 2025-12-16 Severity: Critical

In WebKitGTK-2.50.4, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for memory corruption, crashes (Denial of Service), and arbitrary code execution (ACE). The ACE issue is actively exploited and documented by both Apple and CISA (Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency). These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-14174, CVE-2025-43501, CVE-2025-43529, CVE-2025-43531, CVE-2025-43535, CVE-2025-43536, and CVE-2025-43541.

As the ACE issue is actively exploited and is critical in nature on its own, update IMMEDIATELY to WebKitGTK-2.50.4 or later using the instructions from WebKitGTK (sysv) or WebKitGTK (systemd).

12.4 059 SpiderMonkey Date: 2025-12-16 Severity: High

In SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.6.0esr, three security vulnerabilities were fixed fixed that could allow for sandbox escapes and JIT miscompilations. These vulnerabilities has been assigned CVE-2025-14322, CVE-2025-14324, and CVE-2025-14325.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.6.0esr using the instructions from SpiderMonkey (sysv) or SpiderMonkey (systemd).

12.4 058 Firefox Date: 2025-12-16 Severity: High

In Firefox-140.6.0esr, ten security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for use-after-free operations, sandbox escapes, privilege escalation, JIT miscompilations, same-origin bypasses, and memory safety issues. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-14321, CVE-2025-14322, CVE-2025-14323, CVE-2025-14324, CVE-2025-14325, CVE-2025-14328, CVE-2025-14329, CVE-2025-14330, CVE-2025-14331, and CVE-2025-14333.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-140.6.0esr using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.4 057 Thunderbird Date: 2025-12-16 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-140.6.0esr, ten security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for use-after-free operations, sandbox escapes, privilege escalation, JIT miscompilations, same-origin bypasses, and memory safety issues. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-14321, CVE-2025-14322, CVE-2025-14323, CVE-2025-14324, CVE-2025-14325, CVE-2025-14328, CVE-2025-14329, CVE-2025-14330, CVE-2025-14331, and CVE-2025-14333.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-140.6.0esr using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.4 056 glib Date: 2025-12-08 Severity: High

In glib-2.86.3, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for remote code execution or a denial of service (application crash) when an application uses the g_escape_uri_string() function to escape a URI string. The problem occurs due to a heap-based buffer overflow, and if a string contained a large amount of unacceptable characters, the calculation of the length of the escaped string will overflow and lead to a write off the end of the newly allocated string. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-13601.

To fix this vulnerability, update to glib-2.86.3 or later using the instructions from glib (sysv) or glib (systemd).

12.4 055 c-ares Date: 2025-12-08 Severity: Medium

In c-ares-1.34.6, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a remotely exploitable crash due to a use-after-free problem when reading responses from a DNS server. The process_answer() function could terminate a query after something such as maximum attempts, but it would continue to process additional answers after closing the connection in some cases. The only known impact at this time is an application crash. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-62408.

To fix this vulnerability, update to c-ares-1.34.6 or later using the instructions from c-ares (sysv) or c-ares (systemd).

12.4 054 WebKitGTK Date: 2025-12-05 Severity: Critical

In WebKitGTK-2.50.3, twenty-two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a remotely exploitable denial of service, remote code execution, arbitrary code execution, cross-origin data exfiltration, access to sensor information without a user's consent, information disclosure, sensitive system information disclosure, and cross-origin image exfiltration. These issues are due to a variety of problems including use-after-frees, out-of-bounds reads/writes, buffer overflows, and more. Most of them have been resolved with improved cache, state, and memory handling. All users who have WebKitGTK installed should update immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-43272, CVE-2025-43342, CVE-2025-43356, CVE-2025-43368, CVE-2025-43343, CVE-2025-43392, CVE-2025-43419, CVE-2025-43425, CVE-2025-43427, CVE-2025-43429, CVE-2025-43430, CVE-2025-43431, CVE-2025-43432, CVE-2025-43434, CVE-2025-43440, CVE-2025-43443, CVE-2025-43480, CVE-2025-13502, CVE-2025-13947, CVE-2025-43421, CVE-2025-43458, and CVE-2025-66287.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to WebKitGTK-2.50.3 or later using the instructions from WebKitGTK (sysv) or WebKitGTK (systemd).

12.4 053 urllib3 Date: 2025-12-05 Severity: High

In urllib3-2.6.0, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a trivial remotely-exploitable denial of service. The first vulnerability occurs because there are no limits on the amount of links in a decompression chain, which allowed malicious servers to insert an unlimited number of compression steps (causing extremely high CPU usage and a massive memory allocation for the uncompressed data). The other vulnerability occurs because the streaming API improperly handled highly compressed data in such a way that allowed for urllib3 to fully decode a small amount of highly compressed data in a single operation, leading to massive memory consumption and high CPU usage. Upstream also notes that users who have Brotli installed should make sure that they have updated to 1.2.0. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-66418 and CVE-2025-66471.

To fix this vulnerability, update to urllib3-2.6.0 or later using the instructions from urllib3 (sysv) or urllib3 (systemd).

In addition, users should make sure that Brotli is updated to 1.2.0 or later using the instructions from 12-4.027.

12.4 052 xkbcomp Date: 2025-12-05 Severity: Medium

In xkbcomp-1.5.0, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crashes). One of the issues is due to endless recursion, while the other three are due to NULL pointer dereferences. Two of the NULL pointer dereferences occur in the ExprResolveLhs function, while the other is in the ResolveStateAndPredicate function. All of these vulnerabilities can be exploited by passing an invalid X Keyboard Map to xkbcomp, but the only known impact is a crash of the xkbcomp application. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2018-18583, CVE-2018-15859, CVE-2018-15861, and CVE-2018-15863.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to xkbcomp-1.5.0 or later using the instructions from Xorg Applications (sysv) or Xorg Applications (systemd).

12.4 051 libxslt Date: 2025-12-05 Severity: High

In libxslt-1.1.45, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crashes), memory corruption, or unexpected behavior. All three vulnerabilities can allow for a denial of service, but two of them also allow for type confusion. These two can potentially be exploited through web browsers which process XSLT code inside of stylesheets, and can possibly allow for unexpected behavior if an attacker can corrupt memory. This could potentially allow for remote code execution. It is thus recommended that all users with libxslt installed update to this version as soon as possible. However, special care is required if updating this package on a system with libxml2-2.14.x. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-9714, CVE-2025-7424, and CVE-2025-11731.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libxslt-1.1.45 or later using the instructions from libxslt (sysv) or libxslt (systemd).

On a BLFS 12.4 system which has libxml2-2.14.x installed, this package will fail to configure. The minimum version of libxml2 was increased to 2.15.1. However, this is only needed if you are planning on running the test suite. To work around this, use the following command prior to running configure: sed -i '/LIBXML_REQUIRED_VERSION=/s/2.15.1/2.14.0/' configure. This has been tested on a BLFS 12.4 system. Alternatively, users can update to libxml2-2.15.x, but that may require updates to some packages. The safer option is to just use this sed command.

12.4 050 Unbound Date: 2025-12-04 Severity: Medium

In Unbound-1.24.2, a security vulnerability thought to be fixed by Unbound-1.24.1, but wasn't, was actually fixed that could allow for cache poisoning attacks. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-11411. Please see more information about the vulnerability in SA-12.4-026.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Unbound-1.24.2 or later using the instructions from Unbound (sysv) or Unbound (systemd).

12.4 049 Apache HTTPD Date: 2025-12-04 Severity: Medium

In httpd-2.4.66, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for unintended retry intervals when renewing ACME certificates, for Server Side Includes to unexpectedly pass a shell escaped query string to a command directive, for environment variables to be overridden when using CGI programs, and for users to cause CGI scripts to run under an unexpected username. One additional vulnerability was fixed in this release, but is designed for Windows only. The issue with unintended retry intervals when renewing ACME certificates occurs when using mod_md, and it causes all certificates to attempt to immediately renew repeatedly due to an integer overflow changing the backoff timer to '0'. The Server Side Includes vulnerability requires both Server Side Includes themselves to be enabled, in conjunction with mod_cgid (NOTE: not mod_cgi), and with #exec cmd="..." directives. The environment variable override vulnerability can occur whenever 'mod_cgi' is in use. The CGI scripts running under unexpected usernames vulnerability can occur when mod_userdir is used in combination with suexec while a user also has access to the RequestHeader directive in htaccess. Users who use mod_cgi, mod_cgid, mod_md, or Server Side Includes should update to httpd-2.4.66 immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-55753, CVE-2025-58098, CVE-2025-65082, and CVE-2025-66200.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to httpd-2.4.66 or later using the instructions from Apache HTTPD (sysv) or Apache HTTPD (systemd).

12.4 048 Wireshark Date: 2025-12-04 Severity: Medium

In Wireshark-4.6.2, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash) when processing crafted packets on a network that uses the HTTP/3 or MEGACO protocols. Note that this could be exploitable by a user opening a crafted packet capture file as well. The only known impact though is an application crash, so if you are not processing HTTP/3 or MEGACO protocols, there is no need to update. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-13945 and CVE-2025-13946.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Wireshark-4.6.2 or later using the instructions from Wireshark (sysv) or Wireshark (systemd).

12.4 047 libpng Date: 2025-12-04 Severity: High

In libpng-1.6.52, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for heap buffer over-reads. This vulnerability, unlike previous libpng vulnerabilities, doesn't need a malformed PNG file to be triggered; instead, a valid image can trigger the issue. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-66293.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libpng-1.6.52 using the instructions from libpng (sysv) or libpng (systemd).

12.4 046 SpiderMonkey Date: 2025-12-02 Severity: High

In SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.5.0esr, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for incorrect boundary conditions in the JavaScript WebAssembly component. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-13016.

To fix this vulnerability, update to SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.5.0esr using the instructions from SpiderMonkey (sysv) or SpiderMonkey (systemd).

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-140.5.0esr using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.4 044 Thunderbird Date: 2025-12-02 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-140.5.0esr, nine security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for race conditions, incorrect boundary conditions in the JavaScript WebAssembly component, same-origin policy bypassing, mitigation bypassing, use-after-free operations, and spoofing. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-13012, CVE-2025-13013, CVE-2025-13014, CVE-2025-13015, CVE-2025-13016, CVE-2025-13017, CVE-2025-13018, CVE-2025-13019, and CVE-2025-13020.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-140.5.0esr using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.4 043 libpng Date: 2025-12-02 Severity: High

In libpng-1.6.51, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for heap buffer over-reads, overflows, and out-of-bounds reads. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-64505, CVE-2025-64506, CVE-2025-64720, and CVE-2025-65018.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libpng-1.6.51 using the instructions from libpng (sysv) or libpng (systemd).

12.4 042 CUPS Updated: 2025-12-10 Severity: Medium

In CUPS-2.4.15, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for local denial of services and an unresponsive cupsd process. However, major regressions were found in this update that cause problems with applications hanging. Users who have installed this update should update to CUPS-2.4.16 immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-58436 and CVE-2025-61915.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to CUPS-2.4.16 using the instructions from CUPS (sysv) or CUPS (systemd).

Edited on 2025-12-10 to suggest using CUPS-2.4.16 due to major regressions in the 2.4.15 release.

12.4 041 cups-filters and libcupsfilters Date: 2025-11-22 Severity: Medium

A couple of patches for cups-filters-2.0.1 and libcupsfilters-2.1.1 fixes three security vulnerabilities that could allow for heap buffer overflows and out-of-bounds read access. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-57812, CVE-2025-64503, and CVE-2025-64524.

To fix these vulnerabilities, rebuild cups-filters-2.0.1 and libcupsfilters-2.1.1 with the security patches listed on each page using the instructions from cups-filters (sysv) or cups-filters (systemd) and libcupsfilters (sysv) or libcupsfilters (systemd).

12.4 040 PostgreSQL Date: 2025-11-22 Severity: Medium

In PostgreSQL-18.1, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a check for the schema CREATE privilege being skipped and undersized allocations via integer wraparounds. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-12817 and CVE-2025-12818.

If you are on PostgreSQL-17 and don't want to update your database to 18.x, update to PostgreSQL-17.7 instead using the instructions from PostgreSQL (12.4 sysv) or PostgreSQL (12.4 systemd).

12.4 039 rsync Date: 2025-11-22 Severity: Medium

A patch for rsync-3.4.1 fixes a security vulnerability that could allow for a out-of-bounds heap buffer read through a negative array index. This can happen by a client acting as the reciever of an rsync file transfer who has read access to the remote rsync module. This vulnerability has been assigned as CVE-2025-10158.

To fix this vulnerability, rebuild rsync-3.4.1 with the security patch using the instructions from rsync (sysv) or rsync (systemd).

12.4 038 GnuTLS Date: 2025-11-22 Severity: Low

In GnuTLS-3.8.11, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a stack overwrite. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-9820.

To fix this vulnerability, update to GnuTLS-3.8.11 or later using the instructions from GnuTLS (sysv) or GnuTLS (systemd).

12.4 037 libarchive Date: 2025-11-22 Severity: High

In libarchive-3.8.3, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for temporary file creation in an improper directory and buffer overruns. These vulnerabilities have not been assigned anywhere, but have Github pull requests associated with them: PR #2753, PR #2768, and PR #2769.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libarchive-3.8.3 or later using the instructions from libarchive (sysv) or libarchive (systemd).

12.4 036 Wireshark Date: 2025-11-22 Severity: Low

In Wireshark-4.6.1, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for crashes in the BPv7 and Kafka dissectors. These vulnerabilities have been assigned wnpa-sec-2025-05 and wnpa-sec-2025-06.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Wireshark-4.6.1 or later using the instructions from Wireshark (sysv) or Wireshark (systemd).

12.4 035 Qt6 Date: 2025-11-22 Severity: Critical

In Qt6-6.10.1 and QtWebEngine-6.10.1, twenty-three security vulnerabilities were fixed in that could allow for buffer overflows for both the stack and heap, heap corruption, object corruption, out-of-bounds memory read access, remote privilege escalation, remote read and write files on the filesystem, remote denial of service, remote code execution, domain spoofing, use-after-free operations, information leakage, and sandbox escapes. One of these is actively exploited. Most of the vulnerabilities affect QtWebEngine, but there are some components in Qt6 that are affected by some of the vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-6021, CVE-2025-6965, CVE-2025-10728, CVE-2025-10729, CVE-2025-11206, CVE-2025-11207, CVE-2025-11216, CVE-2025-11219, CVE-2025-11458, CVE-2025-11460, CVE-2025-11756, CVE-2025-12036, CVE-2025-12385, CVE-2025-12429, CVE-2025-12432, CVE-2025-12433, CVE-2025-12438, CVE-2025-12441, CVE-2025-12443, CVE-2025-12726, CVE-2025-13042, CVE-2025-13223, and CVE-2025-24928.

Users are advised to fix these vulnerabilities immediately by updating to Qt6-6.10.1 and QtWebEngine-6.10.1 or later, using the instructions from Qt6 (sysv) or Qt6 (systemd) and QtWebEngine (sysv) or QtWebEngine (systemd).

12.4 034 libsoup Updated: 2025-12-05 Severity: High

There have been several security vulnerabilities found in libsoup-3.6.5. No new release has been made upstream, but the BLFS team has developed a patch to fix the vulnerabilities for which there are patches available. These vulnerabilities can allow for a remotely exploitable denial of service (excessive memory consumption and crashes), for cookie expiration logic to be bypassed (leading to unintended or persistent cookie behavior), for information disclosure in some circumstances, and for arbitrary code execution. The vulnerabilities occur in a variety of different functions and features of libsoup, including the multipart support, the HTTP/2 server, WebSockets support, and more. All users who have libsoup3 installed are recommended to rebuild libsoup with the patch as soon as possible. In addition to the security vulnerabilities, a fix for a potential deadlock when using gstreamer has been resolved as well. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-12105, CVE-2025-4948, CVE-2025-4945, CVE-2025-4969, CVE-2025-4476, CVE-2025-32914, CVE-2025-32908, and CVE-2025-32907.

To fix these vulnerabilities, rebuild libsoup with the patch using the instructions from libsoup (sysv) or libsoup (systemd).

Users that have Epiphany installed should update to Epiphany-49.2 or later to help mitigate the effects of CVE-2025-4035.

Edited on 2025-12-05 now that Epiphany-49.2 is in BLFS.

12.4 033 cURL Date: 2025-11-12 Severity: Medium

In cURL-8.17.0, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a path traversal vulnerability when using the 'wcurl' utility with a URL containing percent-encoded slashes (/ or \). Using percent encoded slashes can trick wcurl into saving the output file outside of the current directory, potentially allowing for attackers to place files in a different place on a user's system without their knowledge. However, this only affects users who are using the 'wcurl' utility - users who are just using libcurl as a build dependency or the 'curl' utility are not impacted. If you are unable to update cURL, a temporary workaround is to pass the '--no-decode-filename' option to the 'wcurl' command any time it is run. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-11563.

To fix this vulnerability, update to cURL-8.17.0 or later using the instructions from cURL (sysv) or cURL (systemd).

12.4 032 Samba Date: 2025-11-07 Severity: Critical

In Samba-4.23.3, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for uninitialized memory disclosure and for command injection in some configurations. Note that the default BLFS configuration is NOT affected, but some obscure configurations may be. The command injection vulnerability is rated as Critical and can occur if a configuration has a WINS server hook script configured. The WINS server used by the Active Directory Domain Controller did not validate user names passed to the WINS hook program, and it passed them by inserting them into a string run by a shell. However, for a system to be affected by this vulnerability, the following conditions must be true:

  • Samba must be configured to run as an Active Directory Domain Controller. The default BLFS configuration is setup for file and print sharing only due to the complexity of configuring Samba as a domain controller.
  • The domain controller must have WINS support enabled.
  • The domain controller must have the 'wins hook' parameter set in the smb.conf file.

The uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability occurs when a server has the streams_xattr VFS object enabled. This is not set in the default BLFS configuration, but may be in some users who have high performance needs. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-10230 and CVE-2025-9640.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Samba-4.23.3 or later using the instructions from Samba (sysv) or Samba (systemd).

12.4 031 Dovecot Date: 2025-11-07 Severity: High

In Dovecot-2.4.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for users to access other users' mail in certain situations. This occurs because of a problem with authentication caching, where the first lookup would be cached for all lookups across the server. This is because the cache key was "%u", which no longer expands to the same as "${user}". This does not affect the standard BLFS configuration as authentication caching is disabled, but if you run a server which has auth cache enabled, you should update your server to this version of Dovecot immediately. Alternatively, you can disable authentication caching. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-30189.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Dovecot-2.4.2 or later using the instructions from Dovecot (sysv) or Dovecot (systemd).

12.4 030 Seamonkey Updated: 2025-11-07 Severity: Critical

In Seamonkey-2.53.22, 18 security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for incorrect error handling of script execution, local code execution, double-free and use-after-free operations leading to memory manipulation and arbitrary code execution (ACE), exposing of persistent UUIDs, partional return value stack writes, truncated instructions, incorrect JavaScript state machines, memory saftey bugs, sandbox escapes, same-origin policy bypasses, integer overflows, out-of-bounds read/write in privileged processes, cross-process information leakage, and non-writable objects being in a writable state. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-5263, CVE-2025-5264, CVE-2025-5265, CVE-2025-5283, CVE-2025-6424, CVE-2025-6425, CVE-2025-8027, CVE-2025-8028, CVE-2025-8033, CVE-2025-8034, CVE-2025-9179, CVE-2025-9180, CVE-2025-9185, CVE-2025-10533, CVE-2025-11709, CVE-2025-11710, CVE-2025-11711, and CVE-2025-11714.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Seamonkey-2.53.22 or later using the instructions from Seamonkey (sysv) or Seamonkey (systemd).

If you are on the version of ICU shipped with BLFS 12.4, please use the same instructions that are in the BLFS 12.4 book for adjusting for ICU.

Updated 2025-11-07 to document changes required for ICU from 12.4, as ICU has been updated in the development books and the sed command is now incompatible.

12.4 029 Xwayland Date: 2025-11-04 Severity: High

In Xwayland-24.1.9, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution or denial of service when using the X11 Present extension, when removing the Xkb resources for a client, and when using the XkbSetCompatMap() function. The X11 Present vulnerability occurs when processing and adding the notifications after presenting a pixmap, because a dangling pointer may be left in the error code path of the XPresentNotify function. This causes a use after free whenever the notification structures are eventually destroyed, causing memory corruption and a subsequent crash. The Xkb client resource vulnerability occurs when removing the Xkb resources for a client. The XkbRemoveResourceClient() function will free the XkbInterest data associated with a device, but won't actually remove the resource associated with it. This causes the resource delete function to trigger a use-after-free when the client is terminated. The vulnerability in the XkbSetCompatMap() function is due to a value overflow, because the XkbCompatMap structure stores some values using an unsigned short, but it fails to check if the sum of the input data might overflow the maximum value. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-62229, CVE-2025-62230, and CVE-2025-62231.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Xwayland-24.1.9 or later using the instructions from Xwayland (sysv) or Xwayland (systemd).

12.4 028 Xorg-Server Date: 2025-11-04 Severity: High

In Xorg-Server-21.1.20, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution or denial of service when using the X11 Present extension, when removing the Xkb resources for a client, and when using the XkbSetCompatMap() function. The X11 Present vulnerability occurs when processing and adding the notifications after presenting a pixmap, because a dangling pointer may be left in the error code path of the XPresentNotify function. This causes a use after free whenever the notification structures are eventually destroyed, causing memory corruption and a subsequent crash. The Xkb client resource vulnerability occurs when removing the Xkb resources for a client. The XkbRemoveResourceClient() function will free the XkbInterest data associated with a device, but won't actually remove the resource associated with it. This causes the resource delete function to trigger a use-after-free when the client is terminated. The vulnerability in the XkbSetCompatMap() function is due to a value overflow, because the XkbCompatMap structure stores some values using an unsigned short, but it fails to check if the sum of the input data might overflow the maximum value. Note that these vulnerabilities can be exploited via TigerVNC as well as SSH X Forwarding, where these vulnerabilities change from arbitrary code execution problems to remote code execution issues. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-62229, CVE-2025-62230, and CVE-2025-62231.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Xorg-Server-21.1.20 or later using the instructions from Xorg-Server (sysv) or Xorg-Server (systemd).

NOTICE TO TIGERVNC USERS: If you have the TigerVNC server configured, you should rebuild TigerVNC with Xorg-Server-21.1.20 or later to protect your systems against these vulnerabilities as well.

12.4 027 brotli Date: 2025-11-04 Severity: Low

In brotli-1.2.0, some security mitigations were put into place that allow for mitigation of unexpectedly large output. This was done by adding in the Decompressor::can_accept_more_data method and the optional output_buffer_limit argument into the Decompressor::process method. Note that this is rated as Low because there is no CVE assigned and this change only affects the Python bindings to brotli, which are not commonly used.

To gain these mitigations for the brotli python bindings, update to brotli-1.2.0 or later using the instructions from brotli (sysv) or brotli (systemd).

12.4 026 Unbound Date: 2025-11-04 Severity: Medium

In Unbound-1.24.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for cache poisoning attacks. The vulnerability occurs because promiscuous NS RRSets that complement DNS replies in the authority section can be used to trick resolvers into updating their delegation information for the zone. Usually these RRSets are used to update the resolver's knowledge of a DNS zone's name servers, but if a malicious attacker is able to attach such records into a reply, the attacker would poison Unbound's cache for the delegation point. Unbound fixed this by scrubbing unsolicited NS RRSets as well as their respective address records from replies, which mitigates this possibility. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-11411.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Unbound-1.24.1 or later using the instructions from Unbound (sysv) or Unbound (systemd).

12.4 025 BIND Date: 2025-11-04 Severity: Critical

In BIND-9.20.15, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for resource exhaustion as well as cache poisoning attacks. The resource exhaustion vulnerability occurs when querying for records which have a specially crafted zone that contains malformed DNSKEY records. An attacker can cause the daemon to consume excess CPU resources until the server crashes. The first cache poisoning vulnerability occurs because BIND is too lenient when accepting records from answers, which allows attackers to trivially inject forged data into the cache. This can happen when any attacker submits a query to a server, and it will affect resolution of all future queries when the data is cached. The other cache poisoning vulnerability occurs due to a weakness in the PRNG that is used, which allows attackers to predict the source port and query ID that BIND will use. This causes BIND to be tricked into caching an attacker's responses if the data is guessed correctly. All users who run a BIND server are recommended to update to BIND-9.20.15 immediately, but there is no reason to upgrade if you are just using the client utilities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-8677, CVE-2025-40778, and CVE-2025-40780.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to BIND-9.20.15 or later using the instructions from BIND (sysv) or BIND (systemd).

12.4 024 libarchive Date: 2025-10-17 Severity: Medium

In libarchive-3.8.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a malicious TAR file to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly other impacts when the contents of the TAR file is listed with a verbose value of '2'. An example provided by upstream is that a 100-byte buffer may not be sufficient for a custom locale. The function impacted is list_item_verbose() inside of tar/util.c. Users who are using libarchive to process TAR files should upgrade to this version of libarchive. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-25724.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libarchive-3.8.2 or later using the instructions from libarchive (sysv) or libarchive (systemd).

12.4 023 Thunderbird Date: 2025-10-16 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-140.4.0esr, 8 security vulnerabilities have been fixed that could allow for use-after-free operations, out of bounds reading/writing, information leakage, modification of non-writable object properties, overriding of browser behavior, potential user-assisted code execution, and exploitation of memory safety bugs. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-11708, CVE-2025-11709, CVE-2025-11710, CVE-2025-11711, CVE-2025-11712, CVE-2025-11713, CVE-2025-11714, and CVE-2025-11715.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-140.4.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.4 022 Firefox Date: 2025-10-14 Severity: High

In Firefox-140.4.0esr, 8 security vulnerabilities have been fixed that could allow for use-after-free operations, out of bounds reading/writing, information leakage, modification of non-writable object properties, overriding of browser behavior, potential user-assisted code execution, and exploitation of memory safety bugs. These security vulnerabilities do not affect the JavaScript component of Firefox (SpiderMonkey). These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-11708, CVE-2025-11709, CVE-2025-11710, CVE-2025-11711, CVE-2025-11712, CVE-2025-11713, CVE-2025-11714, and CVE-2025-11715.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-140.4.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.4 021 gi_docgen Date: 2025-10-14 Severity: Medium

In gi_docgen-2025.5, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for XSS (cross-site scripting) in documentation that gets generated by gi_docgen. The vulnerability was demonstrated in the libsoup API documentation, but can affect other documentation that gets generated by gi_docgen as well. The vulnerability is in the search functionality and allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript code in the context of of the generated website. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-11867.

Additional details on this vulnerability can be found at the upstream bug report.

To fix this vulnerability, update to gi_docgen-2025.5 or later using the instructions from gi_docgen (sysv) or gi_docgen (systemd).

12.4 020 poppler Date: 2025-10-14 Severity: Medium

In poppler-25.10.0, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial-of-service (application crash) when processing a crafted PDF file. This occurs due to a use-after-free, and is due to a common issue that occurs when using raw pointers with elements of a 'std::vector', where dangling pointers can occur when the vector is resized. The vulnerability is in the StructTreeRoot class, particularly in the parseNumberTreeNode function. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-52885.

To fix this vulnerability, update to poppler-25.10.0 or later using the instructions from poppler (sysv) or poppler (systemd).

Two packages in BLFS 12.4 are known to have issues with later versions of poppler at the time of this advisory. Inkscape is known to need a patch with poppler-25.09.0 (which also carries over to 25.10.0). If you are building Inkscape after installing this security update, please follow the instructions from Inkscape (sysv) or Inkscape (systemd). For LibreOffice, you must use version 25.8.3.2 to prevent a build failure. Follow the instructions from LibreOffice (sysv) or LibreOffice (systemd).

12.4 019 Ruby Date: 2025-10-10 Severity: High

In Ruby-3.4.7, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for credential leakage to occur when using the URI gem. This occurs when using the + operator to combine URIs. When using the + operator, sensitive information (including passwords!) can be leaked, which violates RFC3986. This was fixed inside Ruby by updating the bundled URI gem. In BLFS, the only package which uses the URI gem currently is Subversion's Ruby bindings. If you have Ruby installed and are using the URI gem, you should update to Ruby-3.4.7. There is no reason to upgrade otherwise. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-61594, and more details can be found at the announcement from Ruby.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Ruby-3.4.7 or later using the instructions from Ruby (sysv) or Ruby (systemd).

12.4 018 OpenSSH Date: 2025-10-10 Severity: Low

In OpenSSH-10.1p1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for remote code execution in some configurations. Only users who have modified the default configuration in BLFS and set ProxyCommand are vulnerable to the issue, and the issue occurs because OpenSSH allowed control characters in usernames that originate from untrusted sources. If you haven't modified the default BLFS configuration, there is no need to upgrade. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-61984.

To fix this vulnerability, update to OpenSSH-10.1p1 or later using the instructions from OpenSSH (sysv) or OpenSSH (systemd).

12.4 017 fetchmail Date: 2025-10-10 Severity: Medium

In fetchmail-6.5.6, a security vulnerability was fixed that could cause a denial of service (application crash) when authenticating using the SMTP client. The vulnerability occurs due to a failure to validate network input in some configurations. Note that for this vulnerability to be exploitable, a user must have the esmtpname and esmtppassword options configured, as well as the plugout and mda options to be inactive. This particular configuration is rather uncommon, but if you have fetchmail installed with this configuration and are experiencing crashes, update to fetchmail-6.5.6 or later. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-61962.

To fix this vulnerability, update to fetchmail-6.5.6 or later using the instructions from fetchmail (sysv) or fetchmail (systemd).

12.4 016 GIMP Date: 2025-10-10 Severity: High

In GIMP-3.0.6, six security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution when processing DCM, WBMP, FF, XWD, and ILBM files. The ILBM file parsing vulnerabilities occur due to stack-based buffer overflows, the XWD and DCM file parsing vulnerabilities are due to heap-based buffer overflows, and the FF and WBMP file parsing vulnerabilities are due to integer overflows. If you are working with DCM, WBMP, FF, XWD, or ILBM files, you should update to this version of GIMP immediately. Users who update GIMP should also update gegl at the same time. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-10920, CVE-2025-10925, CVE-2025-10934, CVE-2025-10924, CVE-2025-10923, and CVE-2025-10922.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to GIMP-3.0.6 or later using the instructions from GIMP (sysv) or GIMP (systemd).

12.4 015 gegl Date: 2025-10-10 Severity: High

In gegl-0.4.64, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for remote code execution when processing HDR files. Note that this vulnerability is only exploitable via GIMP, which has also seen a security update recently. You should update gegl, and then update GIMP. The issue occurs due to a lack of proper validation of the length of data within an image, prior to copying it to a heap-based buffer. The vulnerability has been classified as a heap buffer overflow. If you are opening untrusted HDR files, it's recommended that you update this package immediately. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-10921.

To fix this vulnerability, update to gegl-0.4.64 or later using the instructions from gegl (sysv) or gegl (systemd).

12.4 014 ffmpeg Date: 2025-10-10 Severity: High

In ffmpeg-7.1.2, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution and denial of service. One of these vulnerabilities is known to be exploited in the wild. These vulnerabilities occur when encoding AAC files, processing MPEG-DASH manifests, and when decoding OpenEXR files. These issues all occur due to heap buffer overflows. Note that ffmpeg is used in several contexts, including in web browsers and media players. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-1594, CVE-2025-59728, CVE-2025-59731, CVE-2025-59732, and CVE-2025-59733.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to ffmpeg-7.1.2 or later using the instructions from ffmpeg (sysv) or ffmpeg (systemd).

12.4 013 QtWebEngine Date: 2025-10-02 Severity: Critical

In QtWebEngine-6.9.3, fifteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, information leakage, and content security policy bypasses. At least three of these vulnerabilities are known to be under active exploitation, and users are advised to update QtWebEngine immediately, even if it is only used as a build dependency. The vulnerabilities are in the libaom, OpenJPEG, V8, File Picker, ANGLE, Extensions, Serviceworker, Mojo, Dawn, and WebRTC components within the bundled copy of Chromium. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-8879, CVE-2025-8880, CVE-2025-8881, CVE-2025-8901, CVE-2025-9866, CVE-2025-10200, CVE-2025-10201, CVE-2025-10500, CVE-2025-10501, CVE-2025-10502, CVE-2025-10585, CVE-2025-54874, CVE-2025-10891, CVE-2025-10892, and CVE-2025-10890.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to QtWebEngine-6.9.3 or later using the instructions from QtWebEngine (sysv) or QtWebEngine (systemd).

12.4 012 OpenSSL (LFS) Date: 2025-10-01 Severity: Medium

In OpenSSL-3.5.4, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for denial of service (application crashes), arbitrary code execution, and private key recovery on ARM64 platforms. One of the denial of service can occur when using the HTTP client API functions, where the 'no_proxy' variable has been set and the host portion of the authority component of the HTTP URL is an IPv6 address. This can also affect the OCSP client functions and Certificate Management Protocol client implementation in OpenSSL. The other denial of service vulnerability (which can also allow for arbitrary code execution) can occur when an application is trying to decrypt CMS messages encrypted using password based encryption. The issue triggers an out-of-bounds read and write. Though the consequences of a successful exploit of the vulnerability can be severe, the chances of an attacker being able to perform it is low, and password-based encryption support in CMS messages is rarely used - which is why upstream marked it as Medium. The private key recovery on ARM64 platforms occurs due to a timing side-channel attack in the SM2 algorithm implementation on ARM64. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-9230, CVE-2025-9231, and CVE-2025-9232.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to OpenSSL-3.5.4 (or 3.4.3) using the instructions from the LFS book for OpenSSL (sysv) or OpenSSL (systemd).

12.4 011 Wireshark Date: 2025-09-30 Severity: Low

In Wireshark-4.4.9, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash) when processing a crafted SSH packet. This can occur both during live packet captures and when reading a previously saved PCAP file. If you are using Wireshark to dissect SSH packets, updating Wireshark is recommended. If you're not using Wireshark to read SSH packets though, there is no need to apply this update. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-9817.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Wireshark-4.4.9 or later using the instructions from Wireshark (sysv) or Wireshark (systemd).

12.4 010 Exiv2 Date: 2025-09-30 Severity: Low

In Exiv2-0.28.7, two security vulnerability were fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash and quadratic resource consumption) when processing EPS files and parsing ICC profiles in JPEG images. The EPS vulnerability occurs due to an out-of-bounds read when calling the Exiv2::EpsImage::writeMetadata() function. The vulnerability can only be exploited when writing metadata to a crafted file, which is done much less frequently than reading metadata. Note that an attacker would also need to convince a user to add extra command-line arguments to the exiv2 command in order to successfully trigger the issue. The ICC profile parsing vulnerability occurs due to a quadratic algorithm in jpegBase::readMetadata(), which is used to read the metadata of a JPEG file. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-54080 and CVE-2025-55304.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Exiv2-0.28.7 or later using the instructions from Exiv2 (sysv) or Exiv2 (systemd).

12.4 009 OpenJPEG Date: 2025-09-30 Severity: Critical

In OpenJPEG-2.5.4, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for remote code execution when processing a crafted JPEG2000 file. The issue occurs due to an unbounded out-of-bounds write, which can occur when the data stream p_stream is too short, and p_image is not initialized. This occurs when processing the header of a crafted image. Note that the vulnerability was originally rated as Medium, but was upgraded to Critical once it was analyzed by NVD. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-54874.

To fix this vulnerability, update to OpenJPEG-2.5.4 or later using the instructions from OpenJPEG (sysv) or OpenJPEG (systemd).

12.4 008 cURL Updated: 2025-11-04 Severity: Low

In cURL-8.16.0, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a predictable mask pattern to occur when using WebSockets (which can allow for a malicious server to induce traffic between machines which can be interpreted by an involved proxy as legitimate traffic), and for sites to overwrite the contents of a secure cookie. The WebSockets vulnerability is classified as "Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers", and requires a libcurl-using application to be communicating through a defective proxy that confuses WebSocket communications for HTTP traffic. WebSocket conections would also need to use clear text rather than TLS (ws:// vs. wss://). The cookie vulnerability has been classified as an out-of-bounds read, and in most cases will result in a crash. In cases where it doesn't crash though, the out-of-bounds read can overwrite the contents of a secure cookie. However, the attacker needs to be in control of an http:// site that uses the same name as a https:// site, or otherwise have MITM capabilities to exploit this vulnerability. The attacker will also have no way to control or guess what is in heap memory following the path buffer, which makes this an extremely fragile operation - which is why upstream has rated the issue as Low. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-10148 and CVE-2025-9086.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to cURL-8.16.0 or later using the instructions from cURL (sysv) or cURL (systemd).

If you install CMake after installing this security update, a minor modification to the source code for CMake is required because of an API change in cURL with this release. The following sed fixes the build failure:

sed -i 's/curl_proxytype/long/' Source/CTest/cmCTestCurl.h

Alternatively, you can update to a later version of CMake to fix the build failure. At the time of writing, CMake-4.1.2 is known to work on BLFS 12.4 systems without known regressions.

Updated on 2025-11-04 to document the problems with compiling the version of CMake in BLFS 12.4 with this version of cURL.

12.4 007 libaom Date: 2025-09-30 Severity: High

In libaom-3.13.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for remote code execution when playing a crafted AV1 file. The vulnerability is primarily known to be exploited in a web browser context, such as in QtWebEngine (with it's embedded copy of Chromium). The vulnerability is classed as a heap buffer overflow. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-8879.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libaom-3.13.1 or later using the instructions from libaom (sysv) or libaom (systemd).

12.4 006 CUPS Date: 2025-09-30 Severity: High

In CUPS-2.4.14, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that can allow for a remotely exploitable authentication bypass and denial of service. If the system is configured with an AuthType set to anything except for 'Basic', the password for a printer or the administration UI is NOT checked if the request contains an 'Authorization: Basic' header. This can allow for a trivial authentication bypass. The denial of service vulnerability occurs due to an unsafe deserialization and validation of printer attributes, and is classified as a null pointer dereference. This is trivially exploitable remotely on systems that are listening for IPP printers through cups-browsed or CUPS itself. Users who have cups-browsed installed or who have modified the configuration for CUPS from the default are recommended to update as soon as possible. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-58060 or CVE-2025-58364.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to CUPS-2.4.14 or later using the instructions from CUPS (sysv) or CUPS (systemd).

12.4 005 Expat (LFS) Date: 2025-09-30 Severity: High

In Expat-2.7.3, a security vulnerability was fixed that can allow for a denial of service (system out-of-memory condition) when parsing a XML document. The issue is known to be exploited easily and reliably. It was fixed by preventing the usage of disproportional amounts of dynamic memory within an Expat parser context. Upstream provides an example where a ~250KiB in size document could cause allocation of ~800MiB from the heap - which amplifies memory consumed by a factor of 3,300. Documents that go past a x100 amplification factor are now rejected with an out-of-memory error. Upstream also notes that a layer of compression around the XML can significantly decrease the minimum attack payload size. Because Expat is used in many contexts, including ones where untrusted input can be processed (such as in a web browser), updating to Expat-2.7.3 is recommended for all users. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-59375.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Expat-2.7.3 or later using the instructions from the LFS book for Expat (sysv) or Expat (systemd).

Note: If you have installed docbook-utils from BLFS you will need to add "--without-docbook" to work around an error in configure, since our installation of docbook-utils uses SGML instead of XML.

12.4 004 PCRE2 Date: 2025-09-29 Severity: Medium

In PCRE2-10.46, a security vulnerability was fixed that can allow for information disclosure and a denial-of-service (application crash) when processing a crafted regular expression.
