This occurs when using the *ACCEPT and *scs: pattern features together, and upstream has noted that the issue can be used to escalate the severity of other security vulnerabilities in a system. The vulnerability is caused by an out-of-bounds read. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-58050.

The handling of this vulnerability requires some special attention. This package was recently moved to LFS at the start of the LFS 12.5 development cycle. Users who update this package will need to use the instructions from BLFS 12.4, while using the new package version instead of the previous version.

To fix this vulnerability, update to PCRE2-10.46 using the instructions from the stable book for PCRE2 (sysv) or PCRE2 (systemd), substituting 10.45 for 10.46 in the URL and instructions.

12.4 003 Thunderbird Date: 2025-09-19 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-140.3.0esr, 7 security vulnerabilities have been fixed that could allow for sandbox escapes, same-origin policy bypasses, exploitation of incorrect boundary conditions, integer overflows, networking information disclosure, and memory safety bugs. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-10527, CVE-2025-10528, CVE-2025-10529, CVE-2025-10532, CVE-2025-10533, CVE-2025-10536, and CVE-2025-10537.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-140.3.0esr or later using the instructions for Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.4 002 SpiderMonkey Date: 2025-09-19 Severity: Medium

In SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.3.0esr, 1 security vulnerability has been fixed that could allow for exploitation of incorrect boundary conditions. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-10532.

To fix this vulnerability, update to SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.3.0esr or later using the instructions for SpiderMonkey (sysv) or SpiderMonkey (systemd).

12.4 001 Firefox Date: 2025-09-19 Severity: High

In Firefox-140.3.0esr, 7 security vulnerabilities have been fixed that could allow for sandbox escapes, same-origin policy bypasses, exploitation of incorrect boundary conditions, integer overflows, networking information disclosure, and memory safety bugs. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-10527, CVE-2025-10528, CVE-2025-10529, CVE-2025-10532, CVE-2025-10533, CVE-2025-10536, and CVE-2025-10537.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-140.3.0esr or later using the instructions for Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

Items between the releases of the 12.3 and 12.4 books

12.3 101 QtWebEngine Date: 2025-08-31 Severity: Critical

In QtWebEngine-6.9.2, 21 security vulnerabilities were fixed that can allow for sandbox escapes, unauthorized user information disclosure, cross origin information leakage, remote code execution, user interface spoofing, arbitrary file read/writes, arbitrary code execution, and bypass of the Content Security Policy (if one is enforced). These vulnerabilities occur in a variety of different components in Chromium, including libvpx, BFCache, V8, Background Fetch, FileSystemAccess API, Compositing, ANGLE, WebGPU, WebRTC, DevTools, Loader, Profiler, Blink, DOM, Filesystems, Cast, and Extensions. Several of these vulnerabilities are extremely severe, but two of them are known to be actively exploited in the wild and are often chained together. These are the sandbox escape and arbitrary file read/write vulnerabilities, which attackers will leverage to implant or read files in a protected area of a user's filesystem, since the sandbox is supposed to tie QtWebEngine to only being able to operate in certain directories on the system. The sandbox escape vulnerability being actively exploited significantly amplifies the severity of all vulnerabilities fixed here. ALL USERS WHO HAVE QTWEBENGINE INSTALLED MUST UPDATE TO 6.9.2 AS SOON AS POSSIBLE, EVEN IF THEY ARE ONLY USING IT AS A BUILD DEPENDENCY. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-5283, CVE-2025-5281, CVE-2025-5280, CVE-2025-5064, CVE-2025-5065, CVE-2025-5063, CVE-2025-8010, CVE-2025-6558, CVE-2025-7657, CVE-2025-7656, CVE-2025-6554, CVE-2025-6557, CVE-2025-6556, CVE-2025-6192, CVE-2025-6191, CVE-2025-5068, CVE-2025-5419, CVE-2025-8582, CVE-2025-8580, CVE-2025-8578, and CVE-2025-8576.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to QtWebEngine-6.9.2 or later using the instructions from QtWebEngine (sysv) or QtWebEngine (systemd).

12.3 100 udisks Date: 2025-08-31 Severity: High

In udisks-2.10.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a local attacker to cause the udisks daemon to crash, or to perform a local privilege escalation by gaining access to files owned by privileged users. This occurs because unprivileged users can create loop devices using the D-Bus interface, and the interface doesn't validate the boundaries correctly, which allows index parameter that specifies where the loop device should be backed to be a negative value. In most circumstances, this will result in a crash, but can be leveraged for local privilege escalation as well. The issue is classified as an out-of-bounds read. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-8067.

To fix this vulnerability, update to udisks-2.10.2 or later using the instructions from udisks (sysv) or udisks (systemd).

12.3 099 MIT Kerberos V5 Date: 2025-08-31 Severity: High

In krb5-1.22.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that causes GSS MIC verification to pass in all circumstances, even if the data provided is incorrect. There are very few details available about this vulnerability, but if you are running a Kerberos server, it's highly recommended that you update to this version immediately to prevent an authentication bypass. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-57736.

To fix this vulnerability, update to krb5-2.22.1 or later using the instructions from MIT Kerberos V5 (sysv) or MIT Kerberos V5 (systemd).

12.3 098 Kea DHCP Date: 2025-08-27 Severity: High

In Kea-3.0.1 a vulnerability was fixed which could lead to a denial of service (assertion abort) sending a malicious request to Kea. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-40779.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Kea-3.0.1 or later using the instructions from Kea DHCP Server (sysv) or Kea DHCP Server (systemd).

12.3 097 SpiderMonkey Date: 2025-08-21 Severity: Medium

In SpiderMonkey-140.2.0esr, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for uninitialized memory access, which can lead to a denial of service (application crash). In order to use SpiderMonkey-140 with the version of gjs used in BLFS 12.3, you must update to gjs-1.84.2 with the spidermonkey_140 patch that is currently in the development version of BLFS. Alternatively, you can update to SpiderMonkey-128.14.0esr. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-9181.

To fix this vulnerability, update to SpiderMonkey-140.2.0esr or later using the instructions from SpiderMonkey (sysv) or SpiderMonkey (systemd).

After installing SpiderMonkey-140.2.0esr, you must update gjs as well with the patch to allow gjs to use the SpiderMonkey-140 series using the instructions from gjs (sysv) or gjs (systemd).

Alternatively, you can update to SpiderMonkey-128.14.0esr with no changes to the instructions necessary.

12.3 096 Thunderbird Date: 2025-08-21 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-140.2.0esr, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a sandbox escape when playing encrypted videos, for a same-origin policy bypass when using 2D graphics, for uninitialized memory to cause an unexpected crash in the JavaScript engine, for a potential denial-of-service (application crash) due to an infinite loop causing out-of-memory conditions in the WebRender component, for spoofing attacks to occur via the Address Bar, and for remote code execution. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-9179, CVE-2025-9180, CVE-2025-9181, CVE-2025-9182, CVE-2025-9183, CVE-2025-9184, and CVE-2025-9185.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-140.2.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

Alternatively, if you wish to stay on the 128 ESR series, you should update to Thunderbird-128.14.0esr using the same instructions.

12.3 095 Firefox Date: 2025-08-21 Severity: High

In Firefox-140.2.0esr, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a sandbox escape when playing encrypted videos, for a same-origin policy bypass when using 2D graphics, for uninitialized memory to cause an unexpected crash in the JavaScript engine, for a potential denial-of-service (application crash) due to an infinite loop causing out-of-memory conditions in the WebRender component, for spoofing attacks to occur via the Address Bar, and for remote code execution. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-9179, CVE-2025-9180, CVE-2025-9181, CVE-2025-9182, CVE-2025-9183, CVE-2025-9184, and CVE-2025-9185.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-140.2.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

Alternatively, if you wish to stay on the 128 ESR series, you should update to Firefox-128.14.0esr using the same instructions.

12.3 094 intel-microcode Date: 2025-08-20 Severity: High

In intel-microcode-20250812, nine security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for privilege escalation or for a denial of service (application crash). The first privilege escalation vulnerability affects all Intel Core CPUs from the 12th generation onwards, as well as some CPUs from the Intel Pentium Gold and Celeron families. The Core i9-1900HX is also listed as affected, and the Intel Core 9 series as well as Core Series 1, 2, and U series are also affected. The Xeon E, Core Ultra, 4th/5th Generation Xeon Scalable, Platinum, Gold, Silver, and Bronze series of CPUs, the Xeon CPU Max series processor, and the Xeon W-2400 and W-3400 processors are also impacted. The rest of the privilege escalation and denial of service vulnerabilities affect the 4th, 5th, and 6th generation of Intel Xeon Scalable CPUs and the W-2400/W-3400 CPUs. Several functionality issues with the 13th generation Intel CPUs and later were also resolved in this update. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-20109, CVE-2025-22840, CVE-2025-22839, CVE-2025-22889, CVE-2025-20053, CVE-2025-24305, CVE-2025-21090, CVE-2025-26403, and CVE-2025-32086.

Additional information about these vulnerabilities can be found at the Intel Security Advisories:

  • INTEL-SA-01249 (CVE-2025-20109)
  • INTEL-SA-01308 (CVE-2025-22840)
  • INTEL-SA-01310 (CVE-2025-22839)
  • INTEL-SA-01311 (CVE-2025-22889)
  • INTEL-SA-01313 (CVE-2025-20053, CVE-2025-24305, and CVE-2025-21090)
  • INTEL-SA-01367 (CVE-2025-26403 and CVE-2025-32086).

Check if your CPU is affected by running lscpu and comparing the outputted family, model, and stepping values with the values provided above and in INTEL-SA-01249, INTEL-SA-01308, INTEL-SA-01310, INTEL-SA-01311, INTEL-SA-01313, and INTEL-SA-01244. If your system is vulnerable, update to intel-microcode-20250812 or later using the instructions from About Firmware (sysv) or About Firmware (systemd).

12.3 093 PostgreSQL Date: 2025-08-16 Severity: High

In PostgreSQL-17.6, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for optimizer statistics to expose sampled data within a view, partition, or a child table; and for arbitrary code execution in the psql client when using the pg_dump command. One of the pg_dump vulnerabilities allows for the superuser of the origin server to execute arbitrary code on client computers, while the other vulnerability allows for newlines in object names to execute arbitrary code in the psql client, as well as in the target server for the restoration of the database from pg_dump. Users who use the PostgreSQL client or server for anything other than a build dependency are advised to upgrade as soon as possible. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-8713, CVE-2025-8714, and CVE-2025-8715.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to PostgreSQL-17.6 or later using the instructions from PostgreSQL (sysv) or PostgreSQL (systemd).

Alternatively, if you are on an older version of PostgreSQL, please upgrade to 16.10, 15.14, 14.19, or 13.22.

12.3 092 ImageMagick Date: 2025-08-16 Severity: High

In ImageMagick-7.1.2-1, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution and crashes when processing PNG and MNG images. These vulnerabilities occur due to undefined behavior, stack buffer overflows, integer overflows, and heap buffer overflows. If you use ImageMagick to perform operations on untrusted MNG or PNG files, you should update to this version immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-53101, CVE-2025-55160, CVE-2025-55154, CVE-2025-55005, and CVE-2025-55004.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to ImageMagick-7.1.2-1 or later using the instructions from ImageMagick (sysv) or ImageMagick (systemd).

12.3 091 Seamonkey Date: 2025-08-15 Severity: Critical

In Seamonkey-2.53.21, sixteen security vulnerabilites were fixed that could allow for use-after-free operations in XSLT, Custom Highlight, WebTransportChild, XSLTProcessor, during concurrent delazification, and the Browser process via AudioIPC StreamData, a buffer overflow, incomplete returns on x86_64 CPUs, sandbox escapes via incorrect handles, privilege escalation in the updater, process isolation bypass, potential local code execution, out-of-bounds access when resolving Promise objects and optimizing linear sums, and memory safety bug fixes. This brings Seamonkey up to date with the security issues fixed in Firefox 115.23.1. If you are using Seamonkey, you should update to this version immediately. These vulnerabilities were assigned CVE-2025-1009, CVE-2025-1010, CVE-2025-1012, CVE-2025-1016, CVE-2024-43097, CVE-2025-1930, CVE-2025-1931, CVE-2025-1933, CVE-2025-1937, CVE-2025-2857, CVE-2025-3028, CVE-2025-2817, CVE-2025-4083, CVE-2025-4084, CVE-2025-4918, and CVE-2025-4919.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Seamonkey-2.53.21 or later using the instructions from Seamonkey (sysv) or Seamonkey (systemd).

12.3 090 glib Date: 2025-08-11 Severity: Medium

In glib-2.84.4, a security vulnerability was fixed that can allow for an arbitrary file write or an application crash. The problem occurs due to a buffer under-read when using the get_tmp_file() function, provided in glib/gfileutils.c. A proof of concept exploit has been published in the upstream bug report, which is now available to the public. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-7039, and more information can be found at the upstream bug report.

To fix this vulnerability, update to glib-2.84.4 or later using the instructions from glib (sysv) or glib (systemd).

12.3 089 7zip Date: 2025-08-10 Severity: High

In 7zip-25.01, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for arbitrary file writes when extracting a crafted file. The reporter of the vulnerability has also noted that depending on the location, it is possible for arbitrary code execution to occur because of this, and they have published a proof of concept that overwrites a user's ~/.bashrc. Note that this vulnerability can be exploited by extracting any kind of file that 7zip supports, and it is not limited to just *.7z files. Another important note is that the vulnerability is rated at Low by MITRE, but MITRE did not take the information about arbitrary file writes into account. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-55188.

To fix this vulnerability, update to 7zip-25.01 or later using the instructions from 7zip (sysv) or 7zip (systemd).

12.3 088 Python (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-08-10 Severity: High

In Python-3.13.6, four security vulnerabilities were fixed in the HTML Parser functionality that can allow for cross-site scripting, denial of service (unbounded resource consumption), and for hidden HTML code to be processed. These vulnerabilities mostly occur because the previous versions of Python did not adhere to the HTML 5 standard correctly. Patches have been made upstream to previous versions of Python, but no new releases have been made at the time of this advisory. If you are using an older version of Python, please use the patches linked at the end of this advisory. No CVEs have been assigned for these vulnerabilities, though they have been requested by the Python security team.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Python-3.13.6 or later using the instructions from Python (sysv) or Python (systemd).

If you are on an older version of Python, please apply the following patches from upstream to your version of Python and then rebuild it:

  • Python PR#136268
  • Python PR#136919
  • Python PR#136273
  • Python PR#135483
  • Python PR#136986
  • Python PR#137171

Please note that the above patches are designed to work with Python 3.12, and that the tarfile vulnerability fix covered in SA-12.3-087 is included in the list. Additional patches may be available for Python versions back to Python-3.9, but these have not been tested by the BLFS team.

12.3 087 Python (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-08-05 Severity: High

A security vulnerability was discovered in Python-3.13.5 that can allow the tarfile module to process tar archives with negative offsets without an error, which would result in an infinite loop and a deadlock when processing maliciously crafted tar archives. Upstream has prepared a patch for the vulnerability which the BLFS editors have turned into a sed. Users who process tar files using the tarfile module in Python should rebuild Python with the sed command to resolve this vulnerability. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-8194.

To fix this vulnerability, rebuild Python using the sed command using the instructions from Python (sysv) or Python (systemd).

12.3 086 WebKitGTK Date: 2025-08-05 Severity: High

In WebKitGTK-2.48.5, ten security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, crashes, sandbox escapes, UI spoofing, internal state disclosure, sensitive user information disclosure, and for download origins to not be associated correctly. Caution needs to be taken if you are on a 32-bit system, or a 64-bit machine with less than 16GB of RAM. If you are on such a system, you are very likely going to run out of memory while compiling. If that occurs, add the CMake options described in the Important section to prevent the system from running out of memory. Performance will be impacted slightly, but not to a level where it is noticable during normal browsing activities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-31273, CVE-2025-31278, CVE-2025-43211, CVE-2025-43212, CVE-2025-43216, CVE-2025-43227, CVE-2025-43228, CVE-2025-43240, CVE-2025-43265, and CVE-2025-6558.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to WebKitGTK-2.48.5 or later using the instructions from WebKitGTK (sysv) or WebKitGTK (systemd).

12.3 085 glibc (LFS) Date: 2025-08-05 Severity: Medium

In glibc-2.42, a security vulnerability was fixed that can allow for a double free when using the regcomp() function. The double free can be accomplished by a malloc failure or by using an interposed malloc that injects random malloc failures, and the double free is known to cause buffer manipulation depending on how the regex passed to regcomp is constructed. All versions from glibc-2.4 to 2.41 are known to be affected. The vulnerability can cause denial of service or arbitrary code execution. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-8058.

To fix this vulnerability, there are two options. One is updating to glibc-2.42 using the instructions from the LFS book at Glibc (sysv) or Glibc (systemd).

IF YOU UPDATE GLIBC, PLEASE FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THAT PAGE ABOUT UPDATING GLIBC VERY CAREFULLY.

Alternatively, a commit was pushed to the release/2.41 branch upstream that is known to fix the issue. If you apply the patch below, ignore the conflict that occurs because of the NEWS file. It has been reported to work by other distributions and verified by an editor. The patch can be found at glibc-2.41 regcomp patch.

IF YOU APPLY THE PATCH AND REBUILD, PLEASE ALSO FOLLOW THE UPDATE INSTRUCTIONS CAREFULLY TO PREVENT A BROKEN SYSTEM.

12.3 084 OpenJDK Date: 2025-07-28 Severity: High

In OpenJDK-24.0.2, give security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, remote information disclosure, and also remotely exploitable denial of service. One of the vulnerabilties is trivial to exploit, but the other four vulnerabilities have a high attack complexity. The vulnerabilities are in the Networking, 2D, JSSE, and Compiler components. None of the exploits require any user interaction or authentication to exploit, and the most serious of the vulnerabilities is the low complexity remote code execution vulnerability in the Networking component. All users who have OpenJDK installed should update to OpenJDK-24.0.2 immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-50059, CVE-2025-30749, CVE-2025-50106, CVE-2025-30754, CVE-2025-30752.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to OpenJDK-24.0.2 or later using the instructions from OpenJDK (sysv) or OpenJDK (systemd).

If you want to use the pre-built binaries, update to Java-24.0.2 using the instructions from Java (sysv) or Java (systemd).

The below information only applies to users who did not update to OpenJDK-24.0.1.

If you install LibreOffice or Fop after this update, you must update to LibreOffice-25.2.3.2 and Fop-2.11 to resolve issues with Java 24's removal of the Java Security Manager API. Links to both pages can be found here: LibreOffice (sysv) or LibreOffice (systemd), and Fop (sysv) or Fop (systemd).

The above updates have been tested against a BLFS 12.3 system.

12.3 083 Qt6 Date: 2025-07-27 Severity: Low

In Qt-6.9.1, a security vulnerability was discovered that can allow for a denial of service when processing a specially crafted ICC profile. The crash occurs when an ICC profile causes a value outside of the expected range to QColorTransferGenericFunction, and this can be exploited by an application using QColorSpace::fromICCProfile to set color profiles. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-5992.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Qt-6.9.1 and apply the patch in the book using the instructions from Qt6 (sysv) or Qt6 (systemd).

Alternatively, you can apply the patch from Qt, which can be found at Qt CVE-2025-5992 Patch for 6.8 and then rebuild Qt, but this has not been tested by the BLFS team.

If you decide to update to Qt-6.9.1, rebuild the following packages if you have them installed:

  • Qca (sysv) or Qca (systemd)
  • qcoro (sysv) or qcoro (systemd)
  • libportal (sysv) or libportal (systemd)
  • Plasma (sysv) or Plasma (systemd)
  • For minimal LXQt installations: layer-shell-qt for LXQt (sysv) or layer-shell-qt for LXQt (systemd).

12.3 082 Apache HTTPD Date: 2025-07-27 Severity: Medium

In httpd-2.4.65, a security vulnerability was resolved that causes all RewriteCond expressions tests to evaluate as true. This vulnerability is caused by a regression introduced with the security fixes in httpd-2.4.64. As a result, all users who updated to httpd-2.4.64 should update to this version immediately. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-54090.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to httpd-2.4.65 or later using the instructions from Apache HTTPD (sysv) or Apache HTTPD (systemd).

12.3 081 Thunderbird Date: 2025-07-22 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-140.1.0esr, fourteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for writing a partial return value to the stack on 64-bit systems, large branch tables leading to truncated instructions, URLs being executed on object and embed tags via JavaScript, cirmcumventing CORS via DNS rebinding, nameless cookies shadowing secure cookies, potential code execution via the "Copy as cURL" command, incorrect URL stripping in CSP reports, XSLT documents bypassing CSP, CSP frame-src not being correctly enforced for paths, search terms persiting in the URL bar, incorrectly handling closed generators via JavaScript, and various memory safety bugs. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-8027, CVE-2025-8028, CVE-2025-8029, CVE-2025-8030, CVE-2025-8031, CVE-2025-8032, CVE-2025-8033, CVE-2025-8034, CVE-2025-8035, CVE-2025-8036, CVE-2025-8037, CVE-2025-8038, CVE-2025-8039, and CVE-2025-8040.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-140.1.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.3 080 Firefox Date: 2025-07-22 Severity: High

In Firefox-140.1.0esr, fourteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for writing a partial return value to the stack on 64-bit systems, large branch tables leading to truncated instructions, URLs being executed on object and embed tags via JavaScript, cirmcumventing CORS via DNS rebinding, nameless cookies shadowing secure cookies, potential code execution via the "Copy as cURL" command, incorrect URL stripping in CSP reports, XSLT documents bypassing CSP, CSP frame-src not being correctly enforced for paths, search terms persiting in the URL bar, incorrectly handling closed generators via JavaScript, and various memory safety bugs. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-8027, CVE-2025-8028, CVE-2025-8029, CVE-2025-8030, CVE-2025-8031, CVE-2025-8032, CVE-2025-8033, CVE-2025-8034, CVE-2025-8035, CVE-2025-8036, CVE-2025-8037, CVE-2025-8038, CVE-2025-8039, and CVE-2025-8040.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-140.1.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.3 079 SpiderMonkey Date: 2025-07-22 Severity: High

In SpiderMonkey-128.13.0, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for writing a partial return value to the stack on 64-bit systems and incorrectly handling closed generators. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-8027 and CVE-2025-8033.

To fix these vulnerability, update to SpiderMonkey-128.13.0 or later using the instructions from SpiderMonkey (sysv) or SpiderMonkey (systemd).

12.3 078 7zip Date: 2025-07-22 Severity: Medium

In 7zip-25.00, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for memory corruption and denial of service. These vulnerabilities occue due to heap buffer overflows and null pointer dereferences. This can occur when processing RAR files or when processing compound documents. The heap buffer overflow vulnerability cannot allow for arbitrary code execution because the bytes past the heap buffer are always oerwritten by zeroes, but a risk of memory corruption still exists. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-53816 and CVE-2025-53817.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to 7zip-25.00 or later using the instructions from 7zip (sysv) or 7zip (systemd).

12.3 077 Ruby Date: 2025-07-17 Severity: High

In Ruby-3.4.5, a security vulnerability was fixed that can allow for a denial of service (application hang) when processing malicious DNS packets that contain a highly compressed domain name. The vulnerability is in the bundled 'resolv' gem, and is caused by an insufficient check on the length of a decompressed domain name with a DNS packet. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-24294.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Ruby-3.4.5 or later using the instructions from Ruby (sysv) or Ruby (systemd).

12.3 076 Apache HTTPD Date: 2025-07-17 Severity: Critical

In httpd-2.4.64, seven security vulnerabilties were fixed that could allow for a denial of service (server crash) when using HTTP/2, for a man-in-the-middle attack to hijack an HTTP session via a TLS upgrade when using the mod_ssl module, for a remotely-exploitable crash when using the mod_proxy_http2 module, for access control bypasses when using the mod_ssl module with multiple virtual hosts, for remote injection of escape characters into error logs when using the mod_ssl module, for server side request forgery when using the mod_headers module to set the Content-Type header, and for HTTP response splitting. The HTTP response splitting vulnerability is a repeat of CVE-2023-38709 because the patch included in httpd-2.4.59 did not actually resolve the vulnerability. Several of these vulnerabilities require unusual configurations, but if you are using mod_ssl, mod_proxy_http2, or the mod_headers module, or HTTP/2 support, you should update to this version immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-53020, CVE-2025-49812, CVE-2025-49630, CVE-2025-23048, CVE-2024-47252, CVE-2024-43204, and CVE-2024-42516.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to httpd-2.4.64 or later using the instructions from Apache HTTPD (sysv) or Apache HTTPD (systemd).

12.3 075 Unbound Date: 2025-07-17 Severity: High

In Unbound-1.23.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for DNS cache poisoning attacks in some configurations. This attack has been called the Rebirthday Attack. The standard BLFS configuration is not impacted as we do not pass the '--enable-subnet' option to configure when building Unbound. However, users who have passed this option to configure are affected. If you did not enable ECS support through passing the --enable-subnet option to configure, you can safely skip this update. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-5994.

Additional information about this vulnerability can be found at the Unbound security advisories webpage.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Unbound-1.23.1 or later using the instructions from Unbound (sysv) or Unbound (systemd).

12.3 074 Bind Date: 2025-07-17 Severity: High

In bind-9.20.11, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a remote attacker to crash the DNS server. If the server is configured with server-stale-enable set to yes and stale-answer-client-timeout configured to 0, and the resolver encounters a CNAME chain involving a specific combination of cached or authoritative records, the daemon will abort with an assertion failure. The standard BLFS configuration is NOT impacted, but if you are running a bind server with the server-stale-enable-set and stale-answer-client-timeout options set, you should apply this update. Users of the standard BLFS configuration or who are just using the utilities can safely ignore this update. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-40777.

To fix this vulnerability, update to bind-9.20.11 or later using the instructions from bind (sysv) or bind (systemd).

12.3 073 libxml2 Date: 2025-07-17 Severity: Critical

In libxml2-2.14.5, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for denial of service and arbitrary code execution when processing a crafted XML file. One of the vulnerabilities affects the xmllint utility, and is a stack buffer overflow. The others affect functionality in the Schematron component, and are type confusion, null pointer dereference, and heap use after free vulnerabilities. Red Hat has marked two of the issues in Schematron as critical. A new release was not cut from the libxml2-2.13 branch upstream, so the BLFS team has crafted a patch for libxml2-2.13.8 that fixes these vulnerabilities via backporting patches from upstream. All users are recommended to update libxml2 immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-6170, CVE-2025-49796, CVE-2025-49795, and CVE-2025-49794.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libxml2-2.14.5 or later using the instructions from libxml2 (sysv) or libxml2 (systemd).

Alternatively, if you are still on libxml2-2.13.x, rebuild libxml2-2.13.8 with the security patch, which can be downloaded from here. This is the recommended method for users on BLFS 12.3 or prior versions as updating to the libxml2-2.14.x series requires several modifications and a complete rebuild of all applications that use libxml2, as it is not ABI compatible with the 2.13.x series.

12.3 072 vim (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-07-16 Severity: Medium

In vim-9.1.1552, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for path traveral when using the tar.vim and zip.vim plugins to view a malicious TAR or ZIP file. It is possible for vim to extract arbitrary files into directories on the system if a relative path is used within the TAR/ZIP file, which can be used to place files necessary to exploit other vulnerabilities on the system. Proof of concept exploits are available for both of these vulnerabilities. If you use vim to view TAR or ZIP files, the BLFS team recommends that you update vim as soon as possible, especially if you are opening files from outside or untrusted sources. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-53905 and CVE-2025-53906.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to vim-9.1.1552 or later using the instructions from vim (sysv) or vim (systemd).

12.3 071 poppler Date: 2025-07-16 Severity: Medium

In poppler-25.06.0, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash), or potentially arbitrary code execution. The problem occurs because of the usage of 'std::atomic_int' for reference counting, and it is possible to overflow the reference count because it is only 32 bits. This bug is classified as a use-after-free. Upstream and the individual that discovered the vulnerability have noted that while there is a chance for arbitrary code execution, the risk is very low as it took as long as 12 hours for them to trigger. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-52886.

Additional information about this vulnerability can be found at the GitHub Security Lab advisory.

To fix this vulnerability, update to poppler-25.06.0 or later using the instructions from poppler (sysv) or poppler (systemd).

12.3 070 GnuTLS Date: 2025-07-10 Severity: Medium

In GnuTLS-3.8.10, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service when processing templates, processing X.509 SCTS timestamps in certificates, when exporting otherName in SAN in a certificate, and when a 2nd Client Hello omits PSK. These vulnerabilities occur due to a buffer overrun, a double-free, a heap read buffer overrun, and a NULL pointer dereference. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-32990, CVE-2025-32988, CVE-2025-32989, and CVE-2025-6395.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to GnuTLS-3.8.10 or later using the instructions from GnuTLS (sysv) or GnuTLS (systemd).

12.3 069 git Date: 2025-07-10 Severity: Critical

In git-2.50.1, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution, for files to be created elsewhere on the filesystem without a user's knowledge, for submodules to unintentionally execute scripts when checking out a module, and for protocol injection when cloning repositories from the internet (when a CDN is configured by the remote server). Two of these vulnerabilities affect Git as a whole, while the other two only impact Gitk. ALL users are encouraged to upgrade git if they have it installed. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-27613, CVE-2025-27614, CVE-2025-48384, and CVE-2025-48385.

Additional information about these vulnerabilities can be found at the Git Release Announcement, Microsoft blog post on one of the Gitk vulnerabilities, and Github blog post.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to git-2.50.1 or later using the instructions from git (sysv) or git (systemd)

12.3 068 PHP Date: 2025-07-10 Severity: High

In PHP-8.4.10, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a remotely exploitable denial of service, SQL Injection, and for Server Side Request Forgery. The SQL Injection issue impacts servers which use the PGSQL extension, and it occurs because the extension does not check for errors while escaping. This is identical to the security issue in PostgreSQL from February 2025, and the PHP component was fixed in this release. The Server Side Request Forgery occurs in the Standard library when processing hostnames, as fsockopen() doesn't regard NULL bytes in hostnames. The remotely exploitable denial of service problem occurs in the SOAP module, and it occurs due to a NULL pointer dereference that occurs when processing large XML namespace prefixes (greater than 2GB in size). These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-1735, CVE-2025-6491, and CVE-2025-1220.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to PHP-8.4.10 or later using the instructions from PHP (sysv) or PHP (systemd).

12.3 067 Thunderbird Date: 2025-07-03 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-140.0esr, ten security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for use-after-free attacks, exposure of persistent UUIDs, Content Security Policy restriction can be bypassed, incorrect parsing leading to allowing embedded of YouTube, ignorance of the Content-Disposition header, DNS request leakage outside a configured SOCKS proxy, singage of a challenge with an invalid TLS certificate, clickjacking via the HTTPS-only exception, Save as action in Devtools not santizing the downloaded files extensions, and exploitable memory safety bugs. Two of the vulnerabilities are rated as High. These vulnerabilities affect browser and browser-like contexts. However, Thunderbird has browser features, so updating should be considered. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-6424, CVE-2025-6425, CVE-2025-6427, CVE-2025-6429, CVE-2025-6430, CVE-2025-6432, CVE-2025-6433, CVE-2025-6434, CVE-2025-6435, and CVE-2025-6436.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-140.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.3 066 gstreamer Date: 2025-07-02 Severity: High

In gst-plugins-bad, a security vulnerability was resolved that could allow for remote code execution or crashes when processing a crafted video file that uses the H.266 codec. The vulnerability occurs due to a stack buffer overflow in the bitstream parser. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-6663.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update the gstreamer stack to 1.26.3 using the instructions starting at gstreamer (sysv) or gstreamer (systemd).

12.3 065 sudo Date: 2025-07-02 Severity: Critical

In sudo-1.9.17p1, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for Local Privilege Escalation. The first vulnerability affects the 'host' option, and requires that a hostname is specified in a sudoers rule to exploit. The '--host' option was only intended to be used with '--list', so that users can list their privileges on a host other than the current machine. However, due to a bug it was not restricted to listing privileges and can be utilized to perform Local Privilege Escalation depending on rules present in /etc/sudoers. The other vulnerability allows an attacker to leverage sudo's -R/--chroot option to run arbitrary commands if the sudoers file allows for the chroot option to work. It's possible to trick sudo to load an arbitrary shared library by creating a /etc/nsswitch.conf file under the user-specified root directory - however note that this again requires non-standard configuration (chroot support) to be enabled. Default installations of sudo on BLFS are not affected, but if you have customized sudoers to add chroot support or to utilize hostnames, you should update to sudo-1.9.17p1 immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-32462 and CVE-2025-32463.

Additional information about these vulnerabilities can be found at the --host security advisory and the chroot security advisory.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to sudo-1.9.17p1 or later using the instructions from sudo (sysv) or sudo (systemd).

12.3 064 Firefox Date: 2025-06-26 Severity: High

In Firefox-140.0esr, ten security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for use-after-free attacks, exposure of persistent UUIDs, Content Security Policy restriction can be bypassed, incorrect parsing leading to allowing embedded of YouTube, ignorance of the Content-Disposition header, DNS request leakage outside a configured SOCKS proxy, singage of a challenge with an invalid TLS certificate, clickjacking via the HTTPS-only exception, Save as action in Devtools not santizing the downloaded files extensions, and exploitable memory safety bugs. Two of the vulnerabilities are rated as High. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-6424, CVE-2025-6425, CVE-2025-6427, CVE-2025-6429, CVE-2025-6430, CVE-2025-6432, CVE-2025-6433, CVE-2025-6434, CVE-2025-6435, and CVE-2025-6436.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-140.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

Alternatively, if you have not compiled ICU-76.1 or above, you can stay on the 128 ESR series and upgrade to Firefox-128.12.0esr.

12.3 063 udisks Date: 2025-06-22 Severity: High

In udisks-2.10.1, a security vulnerability was discovered that can allow for local privilege escalation attacks when chained together with libblockdev and Linux-PAM. The vulnerability occurs because udisks does not always mount filesystems with the 'nosuid,nodev' parameters, which can allow users to escalate their privileges on systems with SUID executables, and this is not supposed to be the default behavior for filesystems mounted via udisks. A detailed proof-of-concept exploit is available with comprehensive exploit documentation. The BLFS developers have implemented a sed to work around the problem. If you have udisks installed on your system, you should rebuild udisks with the sed command in the book immediately. This is part of CVE-2025-6019.

To fix this vulnerability, rebuild udisks-2.10.1 with the sed using the instructions from udisks (sysv) or udisks (systemd).

12.3 062 libblockdev Date: 2025-06-22 Severity: High

In libblockdev-3.3.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for local privilege escalation. The vulnerability occurs due to a bug in udisks, and both packages need to be adjusted to fix the vulnerability. The "allow_active" setting in Polkit permits a physically present user to take certain actions based on the session type. This can be worked around by an attacker abusing a flaw in Linux-PAM (which was fixed in Linux-PAM-1.7.1) to convince udisks to call libblockdev and not mount a filesystem with the 'nosuid,nodev' options - which allows for SUID programs to be run, giving a remote attacker (in the case of the exploit chain that combines this with vulnerabilities in udisks and Linux-PAM) root access to your system. If you have libblockdev on your system, you should update to libblockdev-3.3.1 immediately. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-6019.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libblockdev-3.3.1 using the instructions from libblockdev (sysv) or libblockdev (systemd).

12.3 061 Linux-PAM Date: 2025-06-22 Severity: High

In Linux-PAM-1.7.1, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for privilege escalation and for unauthorized access to systems. The unauthorized access to systems vulnerability occurs in the pam_access module, where certain rules in it's configuration file are mistakenly treated as hostnames. Attackers can leverage that vulnerability to trick the system by pretending to be a trusted hostname, and thus gain access to systems where they are not supposed to have access to. This especially poses a risk for systems that rely on pam_access to control who can access certain services or terminals in a multi-user system. The privilege escalation vulnerability is much more serious and is being chained with vulnerabilities in udisks and libblockdev to achieve privilege escalation to root. There are detailed proof of concept exploits as well as in-depth documentation about exploiting this chain of vulnerabilities, and this vulnerability was disclosed by the French government. All users who have Linux-PAM installed on their systems should update immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-10963 and CVE-2025-6020.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Linux-PAM-1.7.1 or later using the instructions from Linux-PAM (sysv) or Linux-PAM (systemd).

12.3 060 libxml2 Date: 2025-06-21 Severity: High

In libxml2-2.14.4, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service or memory corruption when an application uses the xmlBuildQName() function. Only one package in BLFS is known to use this functionality, and that is PHP. Users who have Wine installed are also impacted as it makes heavy usage of this function. The issue occurs due to an integer overflow in buffer size calculations, which then leads to a stack-based buffer oveflow. The crash happens when processing crafted input. There has not been a new version of libxml2-2.13.x released for this vulnerability, so the BLFS team has prepared a patch for users of BLFS 12.3 to resolve this issue on impacted systems. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-6021.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libxml2-2.14.4 or later using the instructions from libxml2 (sysv) or libxml2 (systemd).

Alternatively, if you are still on libxml2-2.13.x, rebuild libxml2-2.13.8 with the security patch, which can be downloaded from here. This is the recommended method for users on BLFS 12.3 or prior versions as updating to the libxml2-2.14.x series requires several modifications and a complete rebuild of all applications that use libxml2, as it is not ABI compatible with the 2.13.x series.

12.3 059 Xwayland Date: 2025-06-20 Severity; Medium

In Xwayland-24.1.8, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for an integer overflow. It's to ensure that a CVE that was supposedly fixed in the last release is properly fixed. This vulnerability was rated medium. It has been assigned CVE-2025-49176.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Xwayland-24.1.8 or later using the instructions from Xwayland (sysv) or Xwayland (systemd).

12.3 058 Xorg-Server Date: 2025-06-20 Severity; Medium

In Xorg-Server-21.1.18, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for an integer overflow. It's to ensure that a CVE that was supposedly fixed in the last release is properly fixed. This vulnerability was rated medium. It has been assigned CVE-2025-49176.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Xorg-Server-21.1.18 or later using the instructions from Xorg-Server (sysv) or Xorg-Server (systemd).

12.3 057 Xwayland Date: 2025-06-17 Severity; Medium

In Xwayland-24.1.7, six security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for out of bounds reads, integer overflows, old data reads, and a client being able to cause another client to hang. Many of these come from extensions and many of them are very old vulnerabilites, some as old as X11R6. These vulnerabilities are all rated as medium. Said vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-49175, CVE-2025-49176, CVE-2025-49177, CVE-2025-49178, CVE-2025-49179, and CVE-2025-49180.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Xwayland-24.1.7 or later using the instructions from Xwayland (sysv) or Xwayland (systemd).

12.3 056 Xorg-Server Date: 2025-06-17 Severity; Medium

In Xorg-Server-21.1.17, six security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for out of bounds reads, integer overflows, old data reads, and a client being able to cause another client to hang. Many of these come from extensions and many of them are very old vulnerabilites, some as old as X11R6. These vulnerabilities are all rated as medium. Said vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-49175, CVE-2025-49176, CVE-2025-49177, CVE-2025-49178, CVE-2025-49179, and CVE-2025-49180.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Xorg-Server-21.1.17 or later using the instructions from Xorg-Server (sysv) or Xorg-Server (systemd).

12.3 055 Requests (Python Module) Date: 2025-06-13 Severity: Medium

In Requests-2.32.4, a security vulnerability was fixed where a crafted URL and trusted environment can retrieve credentials from the wrong hostname from a .netrc file. Users who do not have a ~/.netrc file with credentials are not impacted by this vulnerability, and there is no reason for them to update to this version. If you do have a ~/.netrc file though, you should update to Requests-2.32.4 immediately, as the workaround requires modifying every requests session to specify "trust_env=False". This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-47081.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Requests-2.32.4 or later using the instructions from Requests (sysv) or Requests (systemd).

12.3 054 Konsole Date: 2025-06-13 Severity: Critical

In Konsole-25.04.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that allows for attackers to trick users into executing arbitrary code with a malicious link. The vulnerability occurs because Konsole allows loading URLs from various scheme handlers (such as telnet://), but it does not check first to see if the program to handle the scheme is present. If it isn't present, it will execute 'bash' instead, allowing for arbitrary code execution. One of the BLFS team members developed a proof of concept that works on BLFS as the rlogin utility is no longer installed on LFS systems, being disabled from inetutils (but still supported by Konsole). There are two ways to fix this: updating to Konsole-25.04.2, or removing the $KF6_PREFIX/share/applications/ktelnetservice6.desktop file. The BLFS team recommends updating the package and it has been tested and confirmed to work on BLFS 12.3 systems. The telnet://, rlogin://, and ssh:// backends are impacted, and you are vulnerable if any one of those three programs are not present on your system. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-49091.

More information can be found from the write-up at oss-security.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Konsole-25.04.2 or later using the instructions from Konsole (sysv) or Konsole (systemd).

Alternatively, you can remove the telnet service by removing the $KF6_PREFIX/share/applications/ktenletservice6.desktop file from your system.

12.3 053 Thunderbird Date: 2025-06-11 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-128.11.1esr, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for credential linkage, disk usage exhaustion, and unsolicited file downloads by using crafted HTML mailbox:/// links. This was the same vulnerability that was claimed to be fixed in Thunderbird-128.10.2esr. Due to different code landing, the vulnerability was never fixed until this release. This vulnerability is rated as high and was unfixed for 22 days. Update immediately. The CVE that was claimed to be fixed was assigned CVE-2025-3877 but has been rejected. The new assignment is CVE-2025-5986.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Thunderbird-128.11.1esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.3 052 Samba Date: 2025-06-09 Severity: Medium

In Samba-4.22.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for file shares to be exposed to clients until client computers disconnect from an SMB server and reconnect again. The problem occurs because the smbd service daemon did not pick up group membership changes when it reset an expired SMB session. This however only affects Kerberos authentication, which is not part of the standard BLFS configuration. Users who are using the standard BLFS configuration are not impacted, nor are they impacted if they are just using the client side components of Samba. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-0620.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Samba-4.22.2 or later using the instructions from Samba (sysv) or Samba (systemd).

12.3 051 libvpx Date: 2025-06-09 Severity: Medium

In libvpx-1.15.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution when processing VP8 and VP9 files, or for a denial of service (application crash). This vulnerability can be exploited in a variety of contexts, including media players and web browsers. The vulnerability was discovered in Google Chrome, but can affect other browsers when viewing webpages. The issue is due to a use-after-free. Note that this update can be challenging to do on a BLFS 12.3 system as several packages will need to be rebuilt, since it is not ABI compatible with 1.15.0. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-5283.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libvpx-1.15.2 or later using the instructions from libvpx (sysv) or libvpx (systemd).

After upgrading libvpx, users will need to reinstall the following packages on their system:

  • ffmpeg
  • VLC
  • gst-plugins-good
  • xine-lib
  • Thunderbird
  • Firefox

12.3 050 File::Find::Rule Date: 2025-06-09 Severity: High

In File::Find::Rule-0.35, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution when 'grep()' encounters a maliciously crafted file name. A file handle is opened with the 2 argument form of 'open()', which allows an attacker provided filename to provide the MODE parameter to open(), turning the filename into a command to be executed. There is a proof of concept available to demonstrate how the vulnerability can be exploited. Users who have File::Find;:Rule installed should update to 0.35. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2011-10007.

More details about the vulnerability can be found at the oss-security post.

To fix this vulnerability, update to File::Find::Rule-0.35 or later using the instructions from File::Find::Rule (sysv) or File::Find::Rule (systemd).

Alternatively, users can use 'cpan to update the module, using: cpan -i File::Find::Rule as the root user.

12.3 049 Wireshark Date: 2025-06-09 Severity: High

In Wireshark-4.4.7, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a crash due to a buffer overflow while processing crafted packets. The crash occurs with many dissectors as it impacts the common Columns module built into Wireshark. The crash can occur while processing a malformed packet trace file, or when capturing packets on a network if an attacker injects a malformed packet into the wire. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-5601.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Wireshark-4.4.7 or later using the instructions from Wireshark (sysv) or Wireshark (systemd).

12.3 048 cURL Date: 2025-06-04 Severity: Low

In cURL-8.14.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for an infinite loop to occur when processing a maliciously crafted WebSocket packet. Upstream has stated that there is no way to exit an affected program other than by killing the process. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-5399.

To fix this vulnerability, update to cURL-8.14.1 or later using the instructions from cURL (sysv) or cURL (systemd).

12.3 047 Python (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-06-04 Severity: Critical

In Python-3.13.4, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service when processing long IPv6 addresses, and for tarfile extraction filters to be bypassed using crafted symlinks and hard links. The extraction filter bypasses allow attackers to write arbitrary files onto a user's filesystem when decompressing a tar file using the 'tarfile' python module. This also officially fixes the unicode-escape vulnerability that was fixed in the security patch that we previously had for Python 3.13.3. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-4517, CVE-2025-4330, CVE-2025-4138, and CVE-2024-12718.

Additional information about the IPv6 vulnerability can be found at the bug report for the vulnerability.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Python-3.13.4 or later using the instructions from Python (sysv) or Python (systemd).

If you are still on Python 3.12, update to Python-3.12.11 using the same instructons.

12.3 046 QtWebEngine Date: 2025-06-03 Severity: Critical

In QtWebEngine-6.9.1, nineteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, information retrieval about peripherals, malicious extension installation, file restriction bypasses, same origin policy bypasses, remotely exploitable privilege escalation, remotely exploitable sandbox escapes, cross origin information leakage, and for access control bypasses. These vulnerabilities are all in the bundled copy of Chromium, and are in the Media, Media Stream, PDFium, Profiles, DevTools, Inspector, V8, libxslt, Navigations, Extensions, Mojo, Codecs, HTML, SQLite, and Loader portions of the package. Most vulnerabilities fixed by this update were rated as High, with two rated as Critical and five rated as Medium. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-1921, CVE-2025-1919, CVE-2025-1918, CVE-2025-1916, CVE-2025-1915, CVE-2025-2136, CVE-2025-1920, CVE-2025-24855, CVE-2024-55549, CVE-2025-3071, CVE-2025-3069, CVE-2025-2783, CVE-2025-3619, CVE-2025-4052, CVE-2025-4051, CVE-2025-4096, CVE-2025-3277, CVE-2025-4609, and CVE-2025-4664.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to QtWebEngine-6.9.1 or later using the instructions from QtWebEngine (sysv) or QtWebEngine (systemd).

12.3 045 MariaDB Date: 2025-06-02 Severity: Medium

In MariaDB-11.4.7, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for unauthorized access to data within MySQL databases, as well as for remotely exploitable crashes. Users who have MariaDB installed as more than a build dependency should update. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-30722, CVE-2025-30693, CVE-2023-52790, CVE-2023-52969, CVE-2023-52971.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to MariaDB-11.4.7 or later using the instructions from MariaDB (sysv) or MariaDB (systemd).

12.3 044 systemd (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-06-02 Severity: Medium

In systemd-257.6, a security vulnerability was fixed that allows an attacker to force SUID processes to crash and allows them to replace the program with a non-SUID binary to access the original privileged process's coredump. This allows the attacker to read extremely sensitive data, such as /etc/shadow content. This can be run by unprivileged users on the system. A proof of concept is public, published by Qualys, that allows for reading the memory contents of the 'sshd' process on some distributions. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-4598.

More details about this vulnerability can be found in the Qualys Security Advisory.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to systemd-257.6 or later using the instructions from systemd.

Users can alternatively upgrade older systems to systemd-256.16 or later. At the same time, users should also upgrade the Linux Kernel on these systems to 6.12.31 or higher because the fix for the vulnerability depends on changes made within the kernel.

12.3 043 coreutils (LFS) Date: 2025-06-02 Severity: Medium

In coreutils-9.6, a security vulnerability was discovered that could allow for a denial of service (application crash) or leakage of sensitive data when using the 'sort' utility. The vulnerability is vulnerable to a heap buffer under-read. LFS 12.3 shipped with coreutils-9.6, but it was later upgraded to 9.7 in the developmenet version of the book. Both versions are affected by this vulnerability. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-5278.

To fix this vulnerability, update to coreutils-9.7 with the patch using the instructions from the LFS book for coreutils (sysv) or coreutils (systemd).

12.3 042 Perl (LFS) Date: 2025-06-02 Severity: Medium

In Perl-5.40.2, a security vulnerability was discovered that could allow for a race condition where file operations may target unintended paths. If a directory handle is opened at thread creation, the process-wide current working directory is temporarily changed in order to clone that handle for the new thread, which is visible from any thread that is currently running. This leads to unintended operations, including loading code and accessing files from unexpected locations, and a proof of concept is available of arbitrary code execution caused by exploiting this vulnerability. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-40909.

To fix this vulnerability, rebuild Perl-5.40.2 with the patch using the instructions from the LFS book for Perl (sysv) or Perl (systemd).

12.3 041 gstreamer Date: 2025-05-30 Severity: Medium

In gst-plugins-base and gst-plugins-good 1.26.2, five security vlnerabilitities were resolved that could allow for remotely exploitable denial of service (application crashes) or information disclosure. The vulnerabilities occur when processing SubRip or TMPlayer format subtitles, as well as when reading crafted MOV and MP4 files. The issues are caused by stack buffer overflows, out-of-bounds reads, and NULL pointer dereferences. The MOV and MP4 vulnerabilties can be exploited remotely in contexts such as web browsers. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-47807, CVE-2025-47808, CVE-2025-47219, CVE-2025-47183, and CVE-2025-47806.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update the gstreamer stack to 1.26.2 using the instructions starting at gstreamer (sysv) or gstreamer (systemd).

12.3 040 ISC Kea (DHCP Server) Date: 2025-05-24 Severity: High

A series of flaws has been made public (along with an update of the server software) by ISC.

  • CVE-2025-32801
    Loading a malicious hook library can lead to local privilege escalation
  • CVE-2025-32802
    Insecure handling of file paths allows multiple local attacks
  • CVE-2025-32803
    Insecure file permissions can result in confidential information leakage

The first two are fixed by the upgrade to at least version 2.6.3. The third one is should be fixed by proper configuration so that data (lease files) and logs are stored in directories which can be made not world-readable.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to kea-2.6.3 or later using the instructions from Kea (sysv) or Kea (systemd) and check the sample configs provided there.

12.3 039 Thunderbird Date: 2025-05-28 Severity: Critical

In Thunderbird-128.11.0esr, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remotely exploitable crashes, memory corruption, remote code execution, cross-origin information leakage, local code execution through the "Copy as cURL" command, and for clickjacking to trick users into leaking saved payment card details. One of the vulnerabilities is rated as Critical, and thus all users should update immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-5262, CVE-2025-5263, CVE-2025-5264, CVE-2025-5266, CVE-2025-5267, CVE-2025-5268, and CVE-2025-5269.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-128.11.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.3 038 Firefox Date: 2025-05-28 Severity: Critical

In Firefox-128.11.0esr, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remotely exploitable crashes, memory corruption, remote code execution, cross-origin information leakage, local code execution through the "Copy as cURL" command, and for clickjacking to trick users into leaking saved payment card details. One of the vulnerabilities is rated as Critical, and thus all users should update immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-5262, CVE-2025-5263, CVE-2025-5264, CVE-2025-5266, CVE-2025-5267, CVE-2025-5268, and CVE-2025-5269.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-128.11.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.3 037 libarchive Date: 2025-05-28 Severity: High

In libarchive-3.8.0, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for crashes and memory corruption when processing RAR archives, TAR archives, and WARC archives. The issues are due to heap buffer overflows, signed integer overflows, and double-frees. No CVEs have been assigned, but more information can be found in the Github bug reports located at: rar: Do not skip past EOF while reading (#2854), rar: Fix double free with over 4 billion nodes (#2598), rar: Fix heap-buffer-overflow, warc: Prevent signed integer overflow, and tar: fix overflow in build_ustar_entry.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libarchive-3.8.0 or later using the instructions from libarchive (sysv) or libarchive (systemd).

12.3 036 Bind Date: 2025-05-24 Severity: High

When an incoming DNS protocol message includes a Transaction Signature (TSIG), BIND always checks it. If the TSIG contains an invalid value in the algorithm field, BIND immediately aborts with an assertion failure. This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.20.0 through 9.20.8 and 9.21.0 through 9.21.7. CVE-2025-40775.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to bind-9.20.9 or later using the instructions from Bind (sysv) or Bind (systemd).

12.3 035 Thunderbird Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Critical

In Thunderbird-128.10.2esr (as well as 128.9.1, 128.9.2, 128.10.0, and 128.10.1), eighteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, URL bar spoofing, arbitrary code execution, leaks of hashed Window credentials, information disclosure of the directory listing of /tmp, UI misrepresentation of attachment URLs, sandbox escapes, remotely exploitable crashes, unsafe attribute accesses (leading to memory corruption and out-of-bounds memory access), sender spoofing (leading to extremely trivial phishing attacks), unsolicited file downloads, disk space exhaustion, credential leakage to remote attackers via compromised emails and attachments, JavaScript execution via spoofed PDF attachments, and tracking links in attachments bypassing remote content blocking. In addition, two of the remote code execution vulnerabilities are the same as what was fixed in Spidermonkey and Firefox, demonstrated at Vancouver Pwn2Own. The breadth of security vulnerabilities in this set of Thunderbird updates should be taken seriously, and similar to Firefox and Spidermonkey, all users who have Thunderbird installed need to urgently update to Thunderbird 128.10.1esr or later. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-3028, CVE-2025-3029, CVE-2025-3030, CVE-2025-3522, CVE-2025-2830, CVE-2025-3523, CVE-2025-4083, CVE-2025-4087, CVE-2025-4091, CVE-2025-4093, CVE-2025-3875, CVE-2025-3877, CVE-2025-3909, CVE-2025-3932, CVE-2025-4918, CVE-2025-4919.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-128.10.2esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.3 034 Firefox Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Critical

In Firefox-128.10.1esr (and 128.9.0/128.10.0), nine security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, URL bar spoofing, sandbox escapes, and unsafe attribute access (leading to out-of-bounds memory access and memory corruption). Most of these vulnerabilities are exploitable via standard web browsing, and two of the remote code execution vulnerabilities are known to be exploited in the wild. The two remote code execution vulnerabilities mentioned were demonostrated at the Vancouver Pwn2Own conference. All users who have Firefox installed must urgently update to Firefox-128.10.1esr to protect their system. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-3028, CVE-2025-3029, CVE-2025-3030, CVE-2025-4083, CVE-2025-4087, CVE-2025-4091, CVE-2025-4093, CVE-2025-4918, and CVE-2025-4919.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-128.10.1esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.3 033 Spidermonkey Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Critical

In Spidermonkey-128.10.1, two critical security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for an attacker to read and write out of bounds memory through executing malicious JavaScript. The first of these vulnerabilities occurs when using 'promise' objects, while the other vulnerability happens due to confusing array index on a JavaScript object. These attacks have been demonstrated to achieve remote code execution and JavaScript manipulation at the Vancouver Pwn2Own conference. All users who have Spidermonkey installed urgently need to update it on their systems. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-4918 and CVE-2025-4919.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Spidermonkey-128.10.1 or later using the instructions from Spidermonkey (sysv) or Spidermonkey (systemd).

12.3 032 Gimp Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In Gimp-3.0.4, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for remote code execution when processing a crafted .ICO file. The vulnerability appears to have been introduced in an early release candidate for gimp3, and is caused by an integer overflow. No CVE has been assigned yet, but there is a Zero Day Initiative ID assigned to the vulnerability. Users who update to Gimp-3.0.4 will also need to update babl and gegl to their latest versions before updating to Gimp-3.0.4. This vulnerability has been assigned ZDI-CAN-26752.

Once the CVE ID is assigned by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative, the security advisory will be updated to include it. Because of the severity (given that it is an RCE), the BLFS team has chosen to file the advisory prior to that portion of the CVE process completing, since all of the data is already public.

To fix this vulnerability, first update to babl-0.1.114 or later using the instructions from babl (sysv) or babl (systemd).

Next, update to gegl-0.4.62 or later using the instructions from gegl (sysv) or gegl (systemd).

Finally, update to Gimp-3.0.4 or later using the instructions from Gimp (sysv) or Gimp (systemd).

12.3 031 OpenJDK Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In OpenJDK-24.0.1, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, arbitrary code execution, and unauthorized data modification. No user interaction or privileges are required to exploit these vulnerabilities. The vulnerabilities are in the JSSE, 2D, and Compiler components. The JSSE and 2D vulnerabilities impact all versions of Java after JDK 8, while the Compiler only impacts JDK 21 and 23. Users who have Java installed for any context are encouraged to upgrade. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-21587, CVE-2025-30698, and CVE-2025-30691.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to OpenJDK-24.0.1 or later using the instructions from OpenJDK (sysv) or OpenJDK (systemd).

If you want to use the pre-built binaries, update to Java-24.0.1 using the instructions from Java (sysv) or Java (systemd).

If you install LibreOffice or Fop after this update, you must update to LibreOffice-25.2.3.2 and Fop-2.11 to resolve issues with Java 24's removal of the Java Security Manager API. Links to both pages can be found here: LibreOffice (sysv) or LibreOffice (systemd), and Fop (sysv) or Fop (systemd).

The above updates have been tested against a BLFS 12.3 system.

12.3 030 Screen Updated: 2025-05-28 Severity: High

In Screen-5.0.1, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a reliable local privilege escalation to root, for leaking of file existence information, for TTY hijacking while attaching to a multi user session, for race conditions when sending signals, and for PTYs to be created world-writable. A serious buffer overflow bug caused by a bad strncpy() was also fixed in this release. Because the default configuration of Screen in BLFS is setuid-root, all systems with Screen installed are impacted by these vulnerabilities, some dating back to Screen releases all the way back to 2025. If you have Screen installed, please update to Screen-5.0.1 immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-23395, CVE-2025-46804, CVE-2025-46803, CVE-2025-46802, and CVE-2025-46805.

Additional information about these vulnerabilities can be found at the oss-security mailing list post where the vulnerabilities were announced.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Screen-5.0.1 or later using the instructions from Screen (sysv) or Screen (systemd).

Updated on 2025-05-28 to include the correct CVE number for the last vulnerability.

12.3 029 intel-microcode Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Medium

In intel-microcode-20250512, eight processor-level security issues were addressed. Six of the security vulnerabilities allow for information disclosure, and two allow for denial of service. The first information disclosure vulnerability can allow exposure of sensitive information in shared microarchitectural structures during Transient Execution, and it can allow authenticated users to enable information disclosure via local access. This affects the 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th generation Intel Core processor family, the Intel Xeon W processor family, the Intel Core X-series processor family, several 11th-generation Core i3s and Celerons, the Xeon E-2300 processor family, the Xeon W-1300 processor family, the 3rd generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processor family, and the Intel Xeon E processor family. The second information disclosure vulnerability occurs due to exposure of sensitive information caused by shared microarchitectural predictor states that influence transient execution for some Intel Core and Atom processors. This includes the 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, and 14th generations of Intel Core CPUs, the Atom P6000 family, the Core Ultra family, the 2nd and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processor family, the Intel Xeon E processor family, the Intel Pentium Gold family, some Intel Celeron processors, and the Intel Xeon 6 processor family. As always, it's recommended to check if your specific CPU is impacted by using the information at the end of this advisory. The next information disclosure vulnerability impacts the Intel Core Ultra family, and alllows for unauthenticated users to enable information disclosure due to incorrect behavior. Authenticated users can also gain access to information due to incorrect initialization of a resource in the branch prediction unit on these CPUS. The denial of service vulnerability happens due to insufficient resource pools in the core management mechanism of some Intel processors, as well as uncaught exceptions in the core management mechanism. This set of vulnerabilities impacts the 12th, 13th, and 14th generation of Intel CPUs as well as the 4th and 5th generation of Intel Xeon processors, the Core Ultra processors (series 1 and 2), the Xeon W processor family, the Xeon E processor family, and the Xeon CPU Max series of processors. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-28956, CVE-2025-20103, CVE-2024-43420, CVE-2025-24495, CVE-2025-20623, CVE-2024-45332, CVE-2025-20012, and CVE-2025-20054.

Additional information about these vulnerabilities can be found at INTEL-SA-01153 (CVE-2024-28956), INTEL-SA-01247 (CVE-2024-43420, CVE-2025-20623, and CVE-2024-45332), INTEL-SA-01322 (CVE-2025-24495 and CVE-2025-20012), and INTEL-SA-01244 (CVE-2025-20103 and CVE-2025-20054).

Check if your CPU is affected by running lscpu and comparing the outputted family, model, and stepping values with the values provided above and in INTEL-SA-01153, INTEL-SA-01247, INTEL-SA-01322, and INTEL-SA-01244. If your system is vulnerable, update to intel-microcode-20250512 or later using the instructions for About Firmware (sysv) or About Firmware (systemd).

12.3 028 PostgreSQL Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Medium

In PostgreSQL-17.5, a security vulnerability was fixed that can allow for a database input provider to achieve temporary denial of service on any platform where a 1-byte over-read can trigger process termination. The issue occurs when performing GB18030 encoding validation, and is classified as a buffer over-read. It affects both libpq and the database server, so client applications are also impacted as well as the server component. Note that in order for this vulnerability to be exploited, the text must fail validation. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-4207.

To fix this vulnerability, update to PostgreSQL-17.5 or later using the instructions from PostgreSQL (sysv) or PostgreSQL (systemd).

For users on older versions of PostgreSQL, versions 16.9, 15.13, 14.18, and 13.21 are available for previous release branches.

12.3 027 LibreOffice Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Critical

In LibreOffice-25.2.2.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that allows for PDF signature forgery when using the adbe.pkcs7.sha1 SubFilter. The bug causes invalid signatures to be accepted as valid, and the vulnerability has been rated Critical by NVD as it meets the criteria of "Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature" and "PDF Signature Spoofing by Improper Validation". All users who use LibreOffice to open PDFs should update to LibreOffice-25.2.2.2 or later, as this could allow for phishing. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-2866.

To fix this vulnerability, update to LibreOffice-25.2.2.2 or later using the instructions from LibreOffice (sysv) or LibreOffice (systemd).

12.3 026 gstreamer Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In gst-plugins-bad-1.26.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that can allow for a crash or remote code execution when processing malformed streams in a video file using the H.265 codec. The issue is caused by a stack buffer overflow that occurs when processing slice headers. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-3887, but the information on it is still reserved. A better source of information is the Gstreamer Security Advisory.

To fix this vulnerability, update the gstreamer stack to 1.26.1 using the instructions starting at gstreamer (sysv) or gstreamer (systemd).

12.3 025 ghostscript Updated: 2025-05-28 Severity: Critical

In ghostscript-10.05.1, nine security vulnerabilities were fixed that could result in remote code execution or arbitrary file accesses. The arbitrary file execution vulnerability occurs due to issues with truncated paths with invalid UTF-8 characters. The remainder of the issues occur due to buffer overflows in various contexts, including processing PDF files, serializing fonts, utilising the BJ10V, DOCXWRITE TXTWRITE, and NPDL devices, and when converting glyphs to Unicode. All users who have Ghostscript installed are encouraged to update as soon as possible. After the release of ghostscript-10.05.0, a new version was released named 10.05.1 which fixes an additional security vulnerability that was not known at the time of this advisory, though the new version was already in BLFS. This vulnerability causes Ghostscript to write passwords for encrypted PDF files in plaintext. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-27835, CVE-2025-27832, CVE-2025-27831, CVE-2025-27836, CVE-2025-27830, CVE-2025-27833, CVE-2025-46646, CVE-2025-27837, CVE-2025-48708, and CVE-2025-27834.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to ghostscript-10.05.0 or later using the instructions from ghostscript (sysv) or ghostscript (systemd).

Updated on 2025-05-28 to include information about CVE-2025-48708, which was already fixed in the book when this advisory was filed, though the vulnerability was not known at the time.

12.3 024 Epiphany Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In Epiphany-48.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that allows websites to trigger URL handlers with no user interaction or warning. If the handler application that is called is vulnerable, remote code execution is possible under the user's current context. Before this release, the browser did not warn users or prevent external URL handler applications from opening without a user's permission. The original release of Epiphany-48.1 introduced two regressions that occured when opening Incognito windows and also when opening downloaded files, so the BLFS team recommends updating to Epiphany 48.3 instead of 48.1. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-3839.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Epiphany-48.3 or later using the instructions from Epiphany (sysv) or Epiphany (systemd).

12.3 023 giflib Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In giflib-5.2.2, several security vulnerabilities were discovered. Only one of them has a functional patch, and the BLFS team has adopted a patch from the OpenMandriva team to resolve the issue. The issue is a heap buffer overflow in the gif2rgb utility, that causes a crash and has a chance to cause arbitrary code execution.
