In addition to the several other issues, this vulnerability has been assigned four different individual CVEs, which are known as CVE-2022-28506, CVE-2023-48161, CVE-2024-45993, and CVE-2025-31344.

Please keep an eye out for future security advisories for giflib as more of the vulnerabilities in this package are resolved.

To fix the four vulnerabilities, rebuild giflib with the patch that the BLFS team has developed using the instructions from giflib (sysv) or giflib (systemd).

12.3 022 libsoup2 Updated: 2025-05-28 Severity: Critical

In libsoup-2.74.3, fourteen security vulnerabilities were discovered that could allow for remotely exploitable crashes, remote code execution, HTTP Request Smuggling, and memory corruption. These are very similar to the vulnerabilities fixed in the recent libsoup3 update, however it includes fixes for several vulnerabilities that are specific to libsoup2. Because of the security vulnerabilities in libsoup2, and the fact that the only packages in BLFS that require it are abandoned, the BLFS team has archived libsoup2 as well as consumers such as AbiWord and libgdata. However, the BLFS team has also developed a patch for libsoup2 to fix these known vulnerabilities for users who have libsoup2 installed. At this time though, we will not be producing further patches for this package to fix further issues after BLFS 12.4 is released, and we recommend that all users who have libsoup2 installed discontinue usage of the library. as well as libgdata and AbiWord. Users who have libsoup2 installed and also have gst-plugins-good installed should rebuild gst-plugins-good with -Dsoup-version=3. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-52530, CVE-2024-52531, CVE-2024-52532, CVE-2025-2784, CVE-2025-32050, CVE-2025-32052, CVE-2025-32053, CVE-2025-32906, CVE-2025-32909, CVE-2025-32910, CVE-2025-32911, CVE-2025-32912, CVE-2025-32914, and CVE-2024-46420.

To fix these vulnerabilities, rebuild libsoup2 with the libsoup-2.74.3-security_fixes-1.patch patch combined with the instructions from libsoup (sysv) or libsoup (systemd).

Updated on 2025-05-28 to add additional text about rebuilding gst-plugins-good with -Dsoup-version=3. Thanks goes to Rainer Fiebig for the information!

12.3 021 libsoup3 Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Critical

In libsoup-3.6.5, ten security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remotely exploitable crashes, remote code execution, and memory corruption. These happen in a variety of functions inside of libsoup3, including append_param_quoted(), sniff_unknown(), sniff_feed_or_html(), soup_headers_parse_request(), sniff_mp4(), soup_auth_digest_authenticate(), and soup_message_headers_get_content_disposition(). The issues occur due to a variety of problems, but include integer overflows, segmentation faults, heap buffer over reads, out-of-bounds reads, NULL pointer dereferences, and double frees. It's highly recommended that all users update to the latest version of libsoup as soon as possible, and stay tuned to the security advisories for further updates as there are many more CVEs that have not yet been resolved upstream as of the time of this advisory. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-32050, CVE-2025-32051, CVE-2025-32052, CVE-2025-32053, CVE-2025-32906, CVE-2025-32909, CVE-2025-32910, CVE-2025-32911, CVE-2025-32912, CVE-2025-32913.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libsoup-3.6.5 or later using the instructions from libsoup (sysv) or libsoup (systemd).

12.3 020 Yelp Updated: 2025-06-22 Severity: High

In Yelp-42.2, a security vulnerability was found that allows help documents to execute arbitrary JavaScript, and also read arbitrary files on the disk. Upstream has not released a patched version to fix this issue, but the BLFS team has adopted patches from upstream to resolve this issue. There is a public exploit and writeup available demonstrating the ability to read a user's SSH Private Key via a crafted help document, and thus ALL BLFS USERS WHO HAVE YELP INSTALLED SHOULD APPLY THE PATCHES AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. The patches resolve the issue by implementing a Content Security Policy through some calls to WebKit that prevents the JavaScript code from being executed. [Updated 2025-06-22]: Upstream has now released updates for yelp-xsl and yelp. Users should update to yelp-xsl-42.4 and yelp-42.3 if they haven't already applied patches to fix this vulnerability. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-3155.

To fix this vulnerability, update to yelp-xsl-42.4 and yelp-42.3 using the instructions from yelp-xsl (sysv) and yelp (svn), or yelp-xsl (systemd) or yelp (systemd).

Updated on 2025-06-22 to include details about yelp-xsl-42.4 and yelp-42.3, which fix this vulnerability. Users should use these versions now instead of using the patches.

12.3 019 xz (LFS) Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In xz-5.8.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for invalid input when decompressing an XZ file to cause a denial of service or potentially arbitrary code execution. The known effects include a heap use after free (causing a crash), as well as writing to an address based on the null pointer plus an offset. Applications and libraries which use the lzma_stream_decoder_mt function are impacted. The vulnerability only gets triggered when decompressing crafted files. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-31115.

To fix this vulnerability, update to xz-5.8.1 or later using the instructions from the LFS book for xz (sysv) or xz (systemd).

12.3 018 Python (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Medium

In Python-3.13.3, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for email header spoofing and a denial-of-service (unbounded memory usage). In addition, another vulnerability was resolved after this release of Python that can cause a crash when using the unicode_escape encoding or an error handler when decoding bytes using the bytes.decode() function. The email header spoofing vulnerability occurs when calling the as_bytes function with the policy=default parameter, and requires the email message to be pre-encoded with RFC 2047 prior to calling the function. The unbounded memory usage issue occurs when writing temporary files with the tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile.writelines() function, and occurs because the writelines() function only checks whether it should roll over after the entire lines iterator is exhausted - leading to massive memory consumption. Only one of these vulnerabilities has been assigned a CVE, and that is the bytes.decode() unicode_escape use-after-free vulnerability. That has been assigned CVE-2025-4516.

More details can be found on the other vulnerabilities by visiting the bug reports on Github: Unbounded growth in SpooledTemporaryFile.writelines() and email: invalid RFC 2047 address header after refolding.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Python-3.13.3 or later and apply the patch from Python (sysv) or Python (systemd).

12.3 017 Perl (LFS) Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In Perl-5.40.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service or arbitrary code execution when transliterating non-ASCII bytes. The vulnerability is caused by a heap buffer overflow, and a subsequent out-of-bounds write. A simple one-line reproducer is public that demonstrates a crash caused by this vulnerability. The Perl developers also backported this to the 5.38, 5.36, and 5.34 series. If your system is old enough to have one of these versions, please update to one of 5.38.4, 5.36.3, or 5.34.3. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-56406.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Perl-5.40.2 or later using the instructions from the LFS book for Perl (sysv) or Perl (systemd).

12.3 016 c-ares Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In c-ares-1.34.5, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow a crash when processing DNS queries where a DNS Cookie Failure occurs, where an upstream server does not properly support EDNS, or possibly on TCP queries if the remote server closed the connection immediately after a response. The crash occurs due to a use after free issue in the read_answers() function in c-ares, and is theoretically exploitable by a remote attacker if the attacker floods the target with ICMP UNREACHABLE packets, but they must control the upstream nameserver. The attack vector is network, but the attack complexity is high. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-31498.

To fix this vulnerability, update to c-ares-1.34.5 or later using the instructions from c-ares (sysv) or c-ares (systemd).

12.3 015 Exempi Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Medium

In Exempi-2.6.6, five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for denial of service (application crashes) or for information disclosure of sensitive memory when processing crafted XMP metadata. The issues are all caused by out-of-bounds reads in the Adobe XMP Toolkit SDK that comes bundled with Exempi. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-30305, CVE-2025-30306, CVE-2025-30307, CVE-2025-30308, and CVE-2025-30309.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Exempi-2.6.6 or later using the instructions from Exempi (sysv) or Exempi (systemd).

12.3 014 libxml2 Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In libxml2-2.14.2 (and 2.13.8), two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could result in a denial of service (application crash) or arbitrary code execution when processing XML documents. One of the issues occurs in the xmlSchemalDCFillNodeTables function in xmlschemas.c, and results in a heap-based buffer under read. To exploit that vulnerability, a crafted XML document must be validated against an XML schema with certain identity constraints (or a crafted XML schema must be used). The other vulnerability is in the Python API and can result in out-of-bounds memory access due to an incorrect return value. It occurs in the xmlPythonFileRead and the xmlPythonFileReadRaw functions because of a difference between bytes and characters. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-32414 and CVE-2025-32415.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libxml2-2.13.8 or later using the instructions from libxml2 (sysv) or libxml2 (systemd).

While users can update to libxml2-2.14, it is ABI incompatible with the libxml2-2.13 series as shipped in BLFS 12.3 and will need many packages to be recompiled, which is why the BLFS team recommends staying on the 2.13 series. If upgrading to the libxml2-2.14 series, you will need to update to several packages from the development version of BLFS, including localsearch and libxkbcommon.

12.3 013 lxml (Python Module) Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In lxml-5.4.0, the bundled copies of libxml2 and libxslt were updated to fix five security vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities are known to cause crashes and arbitrary code execution when processing XML and XSLT documents. The issues occur due to heap-based buffer under reads, stack buffer overflows, out-of-bounds memory accesses, and use-after-free issues. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-55549, CVE-2025-24855, CVE-2025-32414, CVE-2025-32415, and CVE-2025-24938.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to lxml-5.4.0 or later using the instructions from lxml (sysv) or lxml (systemd).

12.3 012 QtWebEngine Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Critical

In QtWebEngine-6.9.0, fifteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for sensitive system data exfiltration, user interface spoofing, remote code execution, arbitrary code execution, and sandbox escapes. The vulnerabilities are in a variety of components in the bundled version of Chromium, including GPU, 7-zip, Network, V8, Browser UI, DevTools, Media, Media Stream, PDFium, WebRTC, and Inspector. All users who have QtWebEngine installed should update to this version regardless of the context that they use it in. However, note that a patch is required to fix a regression, and you must update Falkon afterwards to make it compatible with the regression fix. The regression has to do with GPU Acceleration. The WebRTC issue is known to be exploited in the wild. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-11477, CVE-2025-1426, CVE-2025-1006, CVE-2025-0999, CVE-2025-0996, CVE-2025-0998, CVE-2025-0762, CVE-2025-1919, CVE-2025-1921, CVE-2025-1918, CVE-2025-24201, CVE-2025-2136, CVE-2025-0434, CVE-2025-0445, and CVE-2025-0995.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to QtWebEngine-6.9.0 (with the patch) using the instructions from QtWebEngine (sysv) or QtWebEngine (systemd).

After installing this version of QtWebEngine, you need to update Falkon using the instructions from Falkon (sysv) or Falkon (systemd). The latest version of Falkon is known to build without modifications on a BLFS 12.3 system.

12.3 011 Qt6 Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Low

In Qt-6.9.0, a security vulnerability has been fixed that could allow for a heap buffer overflow when passing an incorrectly formatted Markdown file to QTextMarkdownImporter. The only known impacts at this time are application crashes. Upgrading Qt6 to 6.9.0 on an existing system can cause some impacts with applications, so the BLFS team suggests considering the risk before updating to Qt6-6.9.0. Qt6-6.9.0 changes some private API that causes build issues with libportal as well as with some packages in KDE. If you apply this update on an existing system, you will need to rebuild libportal and KDE Plasma, as well as qcoro and qca (which is standard when reinstalling Qt). If you have LXQt installed with the minimal set of Plasma components, you will need to reinstall the layer-shell-qt package. However, there is an alternative for users who want the vulnerability fix and are willing to stay on Qt 6.8. Qt has published a patch for this vulnerability which should apply to the 6.8 series, but it has not been tested by the BLFS team. The only method tested by the BLFS team has been the upgrade to Qt 6.9.0. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-3512.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Qt6-6.9.0 or later using the instructions from Qt6 (sysv) or Qt6 (systemd).

Alternatively, you can apply the patch from Qt, which can be found at Qt CVE-2025-3512 Patch for 6.8 and then rebuild Qt, but this has not been tested by the BLFS team.

If you decide to update to Qt-6.9.0, rebuild the following packages if you have them installed:

  • Qca (sysv) or Qca (systemd)
  • qcoro (sysv) or qcoro (systemd)
  • libportal (sysv) or libportal (systemd)
  • Plasma (sysv) or Plasma (systemd)
  • For minimal LXQt installations: layer-shell-qt for LXQt (sysv) or layer-shell-qt for LXQt (systemd).

12.3 010 Mercurial Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Medium

In Mercurial-7.0.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for cross-site scripting through the web interface (hgweb). The vulnerability allows attackers to forge a link that would execute JavaScript code in the victim's browser, though in most WSGI implementations, such as mod_wsgi for httpd, it should be trapped and the server should return a HTTP 500 error. Note that this vulnerability is not exploitable on default installations of Mercurial, as you must have the hgweb program installed and running through a website. BLFS users do not need to upgrade unless using the 'hgweb' program, which is not enabled by default. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-2361.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Mercurial-7.0.1 or later using the instructions from Mercurial (sysv) or Mercurial (systemd).

12.3 009 Exim Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In Exim-4.98.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow users with command line access to the server to cause privilege escalation. The issue occurs due to a use-after-free, and it occurs because the pointer for debug_pretrigger_buf is not set to NULL before the buffer is freed by the storage management functions in Exim. In the case of BLFS, even though the Exim daemon drops privileges to the 'exim' user early, it is still possible to escalate to root if the bug is triggered prior to the daemon fully initializing. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-30232.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Exim-4.98.2 or later using the instructions from Exim (sysv) or Exim (systemd).

12.3 008 libarchive Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Medium

In libarchive-3.7.9, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for denial of service (application crashes) or potential memory corruption when processing ZIP or TAR archives. The ZIP vulnerability occurs in the 'bsdunzip' utility, and has been described as 'problematic' as there is a public exploit, but it only allows for crashes of the bsdunzip utility. In that case, the ZIP file can cause a null pointer dereference. The TAR vulnerabilities are both due to heap-based buffer overreads because the TAR reader does not check an strftime return value, and due to issues while handling truncation in the middle of GNU long linknames. The vulnerabilities were fixed in libarchive-3.7.8, but libarchive-3.7.8 introduced a serious regression while processing GNU sparse entries, so libarchive-3.7.9 is recommended to be used instead. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-57970, CVE-2025-1632, and CVE-2025-25724.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libarchive-3.7.9 or later using the instructions from libarchive (sysv) or libarchive (systemd).

12.3 007 WebKitGTK Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: Critical

In WebKitGTK-2.48.2, sixteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could result in unexpected process crashes, cross-origin data exfiltration, memory corruption, cross-site scripting attacks, type confusion (on ARM architectures), and sandbox escapes. The sandbox escape vulnerability is known to be exploited in the wild, and it is thus recommended that users update WebKitGTK immediately. However, caution needs to be taken if you are on a 32-bit system, or a 64-bit machine with less than 16GB of RAM. If you are on such a system, you are very likely going to run out of memory while compiling. If that occurs, add the CMake options described in the Important section to prevent the system from running out of memory. Performance will be impacted slightly, but not to a level where it is noticable during normal browsing activities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-44192, CVE-2024-54467, CVE-2025-24201, CVE-2025-54551, CVE-2025-24208, CVE-2024-25209, CVE-2025-24213, CVE-2025-24216, CVE-2025-24264, CVE-2025-30427, CVE-2025-24223, CVE-2025-31204, CVE-2025-31205, CVE-2025-31206, CVE-2025-31215, CVE-2025-31257.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to WebKitGTK-2.48.2 or later using the instructions from WebKitGTK (sysv) or WebKitGTK (systemd).

12.3 006 Expat (LFS) Date: 2025-05-20 Severity: High

In Expat-2.7.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could result in a crash from chaining a large number of entities. The crash is caused by a stack overflow, and it was resolved by fixing the usage of recursion for general entities in character data, general entities in attribute data, and parameter entities. The crash is very easy to trigger. The vulnerability was fixed in 2.7.0, but 2.7.0 introduced major regressions that caused all calls to the XML_GetCurrentByteCount, XML_GetCurrentByteIndex, XML_GetCurrentColumnNumber, XML_GetCurrentLineNumber, and the XML_GetInputContext functions to cause application crashes anytime those functions were called (which was originally spotted by the XML::Parser Perl module's test suite). All users are encouraged to update to Expat-2.7.1 as soon as possible due to how easy this vulnerability is to trigger. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-8176.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Expat-2.7.1 or later using the instructions from the LFS book for Expat (sysv) or Expat (systemd).

Note: If you have installed docbook-utils from BLFS you will need to add "--without-docbook" to work around an error in configure, since our installation of docbook-utils uses SGML instead of XML.

12.3 005 PHP Date: 2025-03-14 Severity: Medium

In PHP-8.4.5, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for crashes, arbitrary code execution, unauthorized HTTP redirects, authentication bypasses, remote system crashes, and for invalid HTTP headers to be processed. The vulnerabilities exist in the Streams, libxml, and the Core components of PHP. All users who use PHP for web applications are encounraged to update to this version to fix these vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-11235, CVE-2025-1219, CVE-2025-1736, CVE-2025-1861, CVE-2025-1734, and CVE-2025-1217.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to PHP-8.4.5 or later using the instructions from PHP (sysv) or PHP (systemd).

12.3 004 libxslt Date: 2025-03-14 Severity: High

In libxslt-1.1.43, two security vulnerabilities were fixed which could allow for arbitrary code execution and crashes when processing XSL documents. Both of these vulnerabilities are use-after-free bugs. One of them happens when processing XPath context nodes, because in nested XPath evalutions, an XPath context node can be modified but never restored. Functions impacted by this in applications which use libxslt can include xsltNumberFormatGetValue, xsltEvalXPathPredicate, xsltEvalXPathStringNs, and xsltComputeSortResultInternal. The other vulnerability happens in the xsltGetInheritedNsList function, and it is related to the exlusion of result prefixes. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-24855 and CVE-2024-55549.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libxslt-1.1.43 or later using the instructions from libxslt (sysv) or libxslt (systemd).

12.3 003 Thunderbird Date: 2025-03-07 Severity: Critical

In Thunderbird-128.8.0esr, nine security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, remotely exploitable crashes, arbitrary code execution, clickjacking, and for web extensions to be disguised as different elements on a web page. Due to one of the remote code execution vulnerabilities being actively exploited in the wild, and becuase it does not require user interaction, the BLFS team recommends that all users who have Thunderbird installed update to 128.8.0esr as soon as possible. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-43097, CVE-2025-1931, CVE-2025-1932, CVE-2024-1934, CVE-2025-1935, CVE-2025-1936, CVE-2025-1937, and CVE-2025-1938.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-128.8.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.3 002 Firefox Date: 2025-03-07 Severity: Critical

In Firefox-128.8.0esr, nine security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, remotely exploitable crashes, arbitrary code execution, clickjacking, and for web extensions to be disguised as different elements on a web page. Due to one of the remote code execution vulnerabilities being actively exploited in the wild, and becuase it does not require user interaction, the BLFS team recommends that all users who have Firefox installed update to 128.8.0esr as soon as possible. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-43097, CVE-2025-1931, CVE-2025-1932, CVE-2024-1934, CVE-2025-1935, CVE-2025-1936, CVE-2025-1937, and CVE-2025-1938.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-128.8.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.3 001 Spidermonkey Date: 2025-03-07 Severity: High

In Spidermonkey-128.8.0, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution (due to type confusion), as well as arbitrary code execution due to unexpected garbage collection occuring during Regular Expression bailout processing. The unexpected garbage collection vulnerability can also result in inconsistent results and crashes, while the type confusion vulnerability only occurs when using a 64-bit CPU. The type confusion issue occurs due to JIT corruption of WASM i32 return values, where they can pick up bits from leftover memory and they will thus get treated as a different type. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-1933 and CVE-2025-1934.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Spidermonkey-128.8.0 or later using the instructions from Spidermonkey (sysv) or Spidermonkey (systemd).

Items between the releases of the 12.2 and 12.3 books

12.2 097 vim (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-03-07 Severity: High

In vim-9.1.1166, a security vulnerability was fixed that allows for code execution when viewing crafted tar files using vim. This functionality is very commonly used by LFS and BLFS users who are viewing TAR files to examine changelogs for new packages. The vulnerability occurs because the tar.vim plugin uses the ":read filename" ex command line to append "filename" below the cursor position, and it does not sanitize "filename'. It is taken literally from the tar archive, which allows for execution of shell commands. Upstream classifies the issue as HIGH severity, and for LFS and BLFS users who use vim to view tar files, this update should be considered urgent. Note that LFS/BLFS 12.3 shipped with this update and are thus not impacted. This vulnerability is assigned CVE-2025-27423.

To fix this vulnerability, update to vim-9.1.1166 or later using the instructions from vim (sysv) or vim (systemd).

12.2 096 Exiv2 Date: 2025-02-27 Severity: Medium

In Exiv2-0.28.5, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution when a user runs Exiv2 on a crafted TIFF image file. The issue occurs due to a heap buffer overflow, and it is only triggered when writing metadata to an image. The vulnerability occurs in the TiffSubIfd() function. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-26623.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Exiv2-0.28.5 or later using the instructions from Exiv2 (sysv) or Exiv2 (systemd).

12.2 095 libxml2 Date: 2025-02-27 Severity: High

In libxml2-2.13.6, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, arbitrary code execution, and denial of service conditions (application crashes). The first vulnerability occurs due to a stack buffer overflow in the xmlSnprintfElements function, and the second vulnerability occurs due to a use-after-free in the xmlSchemaItemListAdd function. The last vulnerability occurs due to a NULL pointer dereference in the xmlPatMatch function when performing compilation of an explicit child axis. Because of the severity of the two code execution vulnerabilities, it is highly recommended that all users update libxml2 immediately regardless of the context that it is used in. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-24928, CVE-2024-56171, and CVE-2025-27113.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libxml2-2.13.6 or later using the instructions from libxml2 (sysv) or libxml2 (systemd).

12.2 094 Exim Date: 2025-02-27 Severity: High

In Exim-4.98.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for remote SQL injection. Note that this vulnerability does not affect the default BLFS configuration. In order for this vulnerability to be exploited, Exim must be built using SQLite as it's database engine, and the runtime configuration must enable ETRN and enforce ETRN serialization. If you changed the configuration to enable all three of these conditions, you should update to Exim-4.98.1 immediately. For all other users, there is no reason to upgrade. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-26794.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Exim-4.98.1 or later using the instructions from Exim (sysv) or Exim (systemd).

12.2 093 OpenSSH Date: 2025-02-27 Severity: Medium

In OpenSSH-9.9p2, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a man-in-the-middle attack to impersonate any server when the VerifyHostKeyDNS option is enabled, and for a denial of service condition (memory exhaustion) related to the handling of SSH2_MSG_PING packets. The first vulnerabiltiy is very complex to exploit as it requires the attacker to exhaust the client's memory resources first, but if that happens, OpenSSH will not properly verify the server's host key. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-26465 and CVE-2025-26466.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to OpenSSH-9.9p2 or later using the instructions from OpenSSH (sysv) or OpenSSH (systemd).

12.2 092 Xwayland Date: 2025-02-27 Severity; High

In Xwayland-24.1.6, eight security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for denial of service or arbitrary code execution. These issues occur due to a use-after-free of the root cursor, a buffer overflow in the XkbVModMaskText() function, a heap buffer overflow in the XkbWriteKeySyms() function, a buffer overflow in the XkbChangeTypesOfKey() function, an out-of-bounds write in the CreatePointerBarrierClient() function, the usage of an uninitialized pointer in the compRedirectWindow() function, a use-after-free in the PlayReleasedEvents() function, and a use-after-free in the SyncInitTrigger() function. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-26594, CVE-2025-26595, CVE-2025-26596, CVE-2025-26597, CVE-2025-26598, CVE-2025-26599, CVE-2025-26600, and CVE-2025-26601.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Xwayland-24.1.6 or later using the instructions from Xwayland (sysv) or Xwayland (systemd).

12.2 091 Xorg-Server Date: 2025-02-27 Severity; High

In Xorg-Server-21.1.16, eight security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for denial of service or arbitrary code execution. If you are using SSH X Forwarding or TigerVNC server, these vulnerabilities can allow for remote code execution. These issues occur due to a use-after-free of the root cursor, a buffer overflow in the XkbVModMaskText() function, a heap buffer overflow in the XkbWriteKeySyms() function, a buffer overflow in the XkbChangeTypesOfKey() function, an out-of-bounds write in the CreatePointerBarrierClient() function, the usage of an uninitialized pointer in the compRedirectWindow() function, a use-after-free in the PlayReleasedEvents() function, and a use-after-free in the SyncInitTrigger() function. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-26594, CVE-2025-26595, CVE-2025-26596, CVE-2025-26597, CVE-2025-26598, CVE-2025-26599, CVE-2025-26600, and CVE-2025-26601.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Xorg-Server-21.1.16 or later using the instructions from Xorg-Server (sysv) or Xorg-Server (systemd).

In addition, if you have TigerVNC installed, upgrade TigerVNC to handle these vulnerabilities using the instructions from TigerVNC (sysv) or TigerVNC (systemd).

12.2 090 Emacs Date: 2025-02-27 Severity: Critical

In Emacs-30.1, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for shell injection and arbitrary code execution. The first vulnerability occurs in the man.el function, which could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary shell commands on a vulnerable system. The other vulnerability occurs when a user invokes elisp-completion-at-point (for code completion) on untrusted Emacs Lisp source code, which can trigger unsafe Lisp macro expansion that allows for attackers to execute arbitrary code. However, this is also exploitable if a user chooses to enable on-the-fly diagnostics that byte compile untrusted Emacs Lisp source code. If you use Emacs, it's highly recommended that you update this package due to the man.el vulnerability. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-1244 and CVE-2024-53920.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Emacs-30.1 or later using the instructions from Emacs (sysv) or Emacs (systemd).

12.2 089 Wireshark Date: 2025-02-27 Severity: High

In Wireshark-4.4.4, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service condition (remotely exploitable crash) when processing Bundle Protocol or CBOR packets using the Bundle Protocol and CBOR dissectors. Note that this vulnerability is exploitable via packet injection or crafted capture files, but if you are not using either of these protocols on your network, or processing untrusted capture files, there is no need to upgrade Wireshark. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-1492.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Wireshark-4.4.4 or later using the instructions from Wireshark (sysv) or Wireshark (systemd).

12.2 088 PostgreSQL Date: 2025-02-27 Severity: High

In PostgreSQL-17.3, a security vulnerability was fixed that allows for SQL injection and arbitrary code execution. The issue occurs because of how PostgreSQL's string escaping routines handle invalid UTF-8 characters, in combination with how invalid byte sequences within the invalid UTF-8 characters are processed by the 'psql' utility. If you use PostgreSQL as a database server (rather than just the client utilities), it is imperative that you update your server immediately to fix the issue. This vulnerability was responsible for a recent compromise of the United States Treasury. The initial version of this update (v17.3) introduced a regression that broke string length handling routines, so the BLFS development team waited to upgrade until PostgreSQL-17.4 was released. As a result, users should use this version instead. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-1094.

Additional information has been released by Rapid7, who was the group who reported the vulnerability to the PostgreSQL team. This can be found at Rapid7 PostgreSQL Advisory.

To fix this vulnerability, update to PostgreSQL-17.4 or later using the instructions from PostgreSQL (sysv) or PostgreSQL (systemd).

12.2 087 vim (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-02-27 Severity: Medium

In vim-9.1.1115, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a heap use-after-free when redireting the output of ':display' to a register rather than a variable or a file. When this occurs, vim will free the register content before storing the new content data in the register. After that, vim will free the content while shortly after trying to access it, which causes the use-after-free to occur. It has been fixed by skipping any output to register zero when trying to redirect to the clipboard registers '*' or '+'. If you are redirecting the output of ':display' to a register, it's highly recommended that you update vim, but there is no need to if you are not using this function. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-26603.

To fix this vulnerability, update to vim-9.1.1122 or later using the instructions from vim (sysv) or vim (systemd).

12.2 086 Python3 (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-02-12 Severity: High

In Python-3.13.2 (and 3.12.9), five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for hostnames to not be flagged as incorrect when using urlparse, for denial of service conditions (memory exhaustion and crashes) when processing Unicode characters, using the asyncio module, or when using the imaplib module to connect to a malicious server, and for email header spoofing when using the email module. Only two of the five vulnerabilities were assigned CVEs. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-0938 and CVE-2024-12254.

Information about the vulnerabilities not assigned CVEs can be found at the following bug reports: PySys_AddWarnOptionUnicode bug report, email header spoofing bug report, and imaplib vulnerability bug report.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Python-3.13.2 (or 3.12.9 if you are on 3.12.x) using the instructions from Python (sysv) or Python (systemd).

12.2 085 OpenSSL (LFS) Date: 2025-02-12 Severity: High

In OpenSSL-3.4.1 (and 3.3.3), two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a timing side-channel attack while computing ECDSA signatures (which allows for exfitration of a private key in an ECDSA signature), and for RFC7250 handshakes with unauthenticated servers to not be aborted as expected. This issue causes clients which use RFC7250 Raw Public Keys (RPKs) to be vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks because server authentication failures are not detected by clients, and then data can be transmitted in plain text. Note that by default, RPKs are disabled in both TLS clients and TLS servers. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-13176 and CVE-2024-12797.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to OpenSSL-3.4.1 (or 3.3.3) using the instructions from the LFS book for OpenSSL (sysv) or OpenSSL (systemd).

Note that if you upgrade OpenSSL to a new minor version (for example, from 3.3.2 to 3.4.1 or from 3.1.4 to 3.3.3), you will need to rebuild OpenSSH if it is installed and it's earlier than the 9.4p1 release; if you upgrade OpenSSL from 1.x to 3.x, you will need to rebuild everything linked against OpenSSL (including OpenSSH).

12.2 084 Unzip Date: 2025-02-12 Severity: Low

In unzip-6.0-consolidated_fixes-1.patch, a null pointer dereference is triggered and causes a SIGSEGV. The bug appears to be located in the code responsible for handling Unicode strings. This allows an attacker to perform a denial of service and possibly opens up other attack vectors. As the unzip package is no longer maintained, we switched BLFS development to use bsdunzip from the libarchive package as a replacement. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2021-4217.

To fix this vulnerability, install libarchive and replace unzip with a symlink to bsdunzip, using the instructions for libarchive (sysv) or libarchive (systemd). Note that xarchiver is not compatible with bsdunzip, so if you are using xarchiver for handling zip files, you'll also need to disable the "Prefer unzip for zip files" option in the "Action => Preferences" dialog, and install 7zip using the instructions for 7zip (sysv) or 7zip (systemd).

12.2 083 Intel Microcode Date: 2025-02-11 Severity: High

In intel-microcode-20250211, twelve total security vulnerabilities were fixed. The first of these vulnerabilities allows for a privileged user to cause a denial of service via local access on 12th-generation Intel Core CPUs and higher and the 4th/5th generation of Intel Xeon Scalable CPUs. It is caused by an error related to improper finite state machines in the hardware logic on those processors. The next of these vulnerabilities allows for a potential denial of service due to an issue with the EDECCSSA user leaf function in the Intel Software Guard Extensions on some 8th, 9th, and 11th generation Intel CPUs, as well as the 3rd generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors, the Xeon D processors, and the 4th generation of Intel Xeon CPUs (belonging to the Eagle Stream family). The next eight of the vulnerabilities allow for privilege escalation, denial of service, and information disclosure due to severe flaws in the UEFI firmware for the 12th and 13th generation Intel Core CPUs, the Core Ultra family of CPUs, the Xeon Processor D family, the 3rd Generation Intel Xeon family, the Pentium Silver, Celeron J, and Celeron N series of chips, the Pentium Gold family, the 1st-4th generation of Intel Xeon Scalable CPUs, the Core X series CPUs, the Xeon-W 2100/2200/2400/3400 series of CPUs, the Atom C5000 and P5000 series of CPUs, and the Atom Processor X series of CPUs. If you are running an affected chip from the families listed above, you should update your microcode as soon as possible. The next vulnerability allows for a denial of service in the 13th and 14th generation of Intel CPUs, where improper handling of physical or environmental conditions in some of these processors may allow an authenticated user to cause a crash. The final security vulnerability impacts the 4th Generation Intel Xeon series of CPUs, the Xeon W workstation processor line, the 5th generation of Intel Xeon Scalable procesors, the Sierra Forest Xeon with 6 E-Cores, and the Atom P9600 processor, and it allows for a denial of service caused by invalid sequences of processor instructions when using Intel Data Streaming Accelerator. Upgrading the microcode, or system firmware, on systems with an 8th-generation Intel CPU or higher is recommended to resolve these security vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-31068, CVE-2024-36293, CVE-2023-43758, CVE-2023-34440, CVE-2024-24582, CVE-2024-29214, CVE-2024-28127, CVE-2024-39279, CVE-2024-31157, CVE-2024-28047, CVE-2024-39355, and CVE-2024-37020.

Additional information can be found in the Intel security advisories themselves: Intel-SA-01166 (CVE-2024-31068), Intel-SA-01213 (CVE-2024-36293), Intel-SA-01139 (CVE-2023-43758, CVE-2023-34440, CVE-2024-24582, CVE-2024-29214, CVE-2024-28127, CVE-2024-39279, CVE-2024-31157, and CVE-2024-28047), Intel-SA-01228 (CVE-2024-39355), and Intel-SA-01194 (CVE-2024-37020)..

Check if your CPU is affected by running lscpu and comparing the outputted family, model, and stepping values with the values provided above and in Intel-SA-01166, Intel-SA-01213, Intel-SA-01139, Intel-SA-01228, and Intel-SA-01194. If your system is vulnerable, update to intel-microcode-20250211 or later using the instructions for About Firmware (sysv) or About Firmware (systemd).

12.2 082 WebKitGTK Date: 2025-02-09 Severity: Critical

In WebKitGTK-2.46.6, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a maliciously crafted webpage to fingerprint a user, for command injection when copying URLs from the Web Inspector, for denial of service, and unexpected process crashes. The user fingerprinting was resolved with improved access restrictions to the filesystem, and the URL copying issue was fixed with improved handling of files. The denial of service and unexpected process crashing issues were fixed with improved memory handling and state management. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-24143, CVE-2025-24150, CVE-2025-24158, and CVE-2025-24162.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to WebKitGTK-2.46.6 or later using the instructions from WebKitGTK (sysv) or WebKitGTK (systemd).

12.2 081 GnuTLS Date: 2025-02-09 Severity: Medium

In GnuTLS-3.8.9, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a potential denial of service to occur when handling certificates with a very large number of name constraints. This is a follow up of the libtasn1 update, and users who have updated to libtasn1-4.20.0 should also update to this version of GnuTLS for additional protection. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-12243.

To fix this vulnerability, update to GnuTLS-3.8.9 or later using the instructions from GnuTLS (sysv) or GnuTLS (systemd).

12.2 080 Firefox Date: 2025-02-06 Severity: Critical

In Firefox-128.7.0esr, nine security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, memory corruption, remotely exploitable crashes, invalid certificate validation, and for potentially opening private browsing tabs in normal browsing windows. The certificate validation issue in particular occurs due to the length of a certificate added to the certificate store not being checked properly. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-1009, CVE-2025-1010, CVE-2025-1011, CVE-2025-1012, CVE-2024-11704, CVE-2025-1013, CVE-2025-1014, CVE-2025-1016, and CVE-2025-1017.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-128.7.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.2 079 Thunderbird Date: 2025-02-06 Severity: Critical

In Thunderbird-128.7.0esr, eleven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remotely exploitable crashes, remote code execution, memory corruption, privacy leaks, certificate validation issues, automatic launching of web pages within Thunderbird, and for email address spoofing. The crashes happen when processing XSLT data, using the custom Highlight API, generating WebAssembly code, processing PKCS#7 certificates, and opening crafted mails. The remote code execution issues occur when opening crafted mails as well. The privacy leaks occur because private browsing tabs could've been accidentally opened in normal browsing windows. The certificate validation issues occur because certificate length was not properly checked when a certificate was added to a certificate store. The launching of web pages in Thunderbird issue occurs because the Thunderbird Address Book URI fields are not sanitized, and attackers can generate and export address book entries that, when a user imports them, can open a web page within Thunderbird and execute JavaScript. The spoofing issue occurs because Thunderbird displayed an incorrect sender address if the From field of an email used invalid group name syntax, similar to CVE-2024-40940. This particular vulnerability can be used to cause phishing attacks, where an unsuspecting user who doesn't look at mail headers can be tricked into thinking that the mail came from a legitimate source (including the correct domain name for a service), even though the email was not sent from that address. All users who have Thunderbird installed are recommended to update it immediately because of this issue in particular. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-1009, CVE-2025-1010, CVE-2025-1011, CVE-2025-1012, CVE-2024-11704, CVE-2025-1013, CVE-2025-1014, CVE-2025-1015, CVE-2025-0510, CVE-2025-1016, and CVE-2025-1017.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-128.7.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.2 078 cURL Date: 2025-02-06 Severity: Low

In cURL-8.12.0, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for denial of service condition (application crash) and for credential leaks in exceptionally rare circumstances. The denial of service vulnerability occurs due to libcurl closing the same eventfd file descriptor twice when taking down a connection channel after having completed a threaded name resolve. There are several conditions that must be true to exploit this vulnerability, including the use of a 64-bit system, cURL being built with the --enable-threaded-resolver option, and that eventfd is used in the cURL build. This can lead to strange crashes in many different applications, but BLFS users must pass --enable-threaded-resolver to cURL's configure script to be affected by it. The credential leak vulnerability is very similar to CVE-2024-11053, and requires the use of a .netrc file for credentials, following HTTP redirects, while the .netrc file has a default entry that omits both the username and the password for a service. Most users will not be affected by this, and a default entry omitting the username and password fields is a rare misconfiguration. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-0665 and CVE-2025-0167.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to cURL-8.12.0 or later using the instructions from cURL (sysv) or cURL (systemd).

12.2 077 libtasn1 Date: 2025-02-06 Severity: Medium

In libtasn1-4.20.0, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service (application crash and timeout) when processing certificates. When an input DER data contains a large number of SEQUENCE OF or SET OF elements, decoding the data and launching a specific element in it will take a quadratic amount of time to complete. This can be utilized by a remote attacker for a denial of service attack by presenting a malicious certificate to the network peer. This can impact any application which uses libtasn1 for certificate parsing and validation. A temporary workaround suggested by upstream is to use resource control mechanisms such as cgroups to help avoid excessive usage of CPU time, but the BLFS team recommends updating libtasn1 instead. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-12133.

To fix this vulnerability, update to libtasn1-4.20.0 or later using the instructions from libtasn1 (sysv) or libtasn1 (systemd).

12.2 076 MariaDB Date: 2025-02-06 Severity: Medium

In MariaDB-11.4.5, a security vulnerabiliy was fixed that could allow for a remote attacker with high privileges to cause a denial of service ( hang and frequently repeatable crash) of the mariadb server. Note that this vulnerability, while extremely easy to exploit, requires the attacker to have network access to the server, which is disabled by default in the configuration provided by BLFS. However, if you have deviated from the book by commenting the "skip-networking" flag in /etc/mariadb/my.cnf, you may be affected by this vulnerability. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-21490.

To fix this vulnerability, update to MariaDB-11.4.5 or later using the instructions from MariaDB (sysv) or MariaDB (systemd).

If you are upgrading from a previous major version of MariaDB, you will need to run the "mariadb-upgrade" command after you have upgraded this package. In addition, you should follow the instructions from the development books carefully, as the flags passed to CMake regarding paths have been changed significantly.

If you wish to stay on the previous major version of MariaDB, please upgrade to MariaDB-10.11.11 instead, but note that BLFS 12.3 will be shipping with MariaDB-11.4.x and we will not support the 10.11 series after BLFS 12.3 is released.

12.2 075 QtWebEngine Date: 2025-02-02 Severity: High

In QtWebEngine-6.8.2, nine security vulnerabilities were fixed which could allow for remote code execution, arbitrary code execution in a sandbox, privilege escalation, and sensitive system information disclosure. These vulnerabilities occur in the Compositing, V8, Metrics, Navigation, Fenced Frames, Extensions, Tracing, and Skia components of the bundled copy of Chromium. All of these issues can be exploited via maliciously crafted web content (including pages and embedded videos). These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-12694, CVE-2024-12693, CVE-2025-0611, CVE-2025-0437, CVE-2025-0447, CVE-2025-0441, CVE-2025-0443, CVE-2025-0438, and CVE-2025-0436.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to QtWebEngine-6.8.2 or later using the instructions from QtWebEngine (sysv) or QtWebEngine (systemd).

12.2 074 Qt6 Date: 2025-02-02 Severity: Medium

In Qt6-6.8.2, a security vulnerability was fixed which could allow for a crash when a Bluetooth Low Energy device pairs and sends malformed Bluetooth ATT commmands to the computer. Note that this impacts the Bluetooth module within QtConnectivity (QLowEnergyController) in particular, and users are only impacted if they use a Qt application to pair with a malicious device. The malformed ATT commands allow for a remotely exploitable crash, and the user must explicitly pair with the device first. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-23050.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Qt6-6.8.2 or later uisng the instructions from Qt6 (sysv) or Qt6 (systemd).

12.2 073 vim (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-02-02 Severity: Medium

In vim-9.1.1071, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a crash when the win_line() function is called in some extreme circumstances. In order to exploit the vulnerability, a user has to be in silent Ex mode (-s -e), and binary characters have to be fed to vim that cause the screen to scroll. This will cause a screen redraw to be triggered even though no screen is present, and thus the ScreenLines pointer is accessed even though the variable is not allocated. The vulnerability was fixed by skipping the redraw attempt by testing whether the ScreenLines pointer is NULL. Note that the impact is medium because the user must intentionally and explicitly feed binary data to vim while also in ex mode. The vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-24014.

To fix this vulnerability, update to vim-9.1.1071 or later using the instructions from vim (sysv) or vim (systemd).

12.2 072 Glibc (LFS) Date: 2025-02-02 Severity: Medium

In Glibc-2.41, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a buffer overflow when printing assertion failure messages. This can allow for application crashes, or in some extreme cases, undefined behavior. The only viable vector for exploitation of this vulnerability is local, and it must be a setuid program that has an existing bug which results in the assertion failure. At this time, the LFS team (and upstream) are not aware of any applications that may have this behavior, but users may have custom setuid programs which can be exploited. This issue occurs due to the assert() function not allocating enough space for the assertion failure message string and size information in some cases, which can lead to the overflow if the message string size aligns to page size. For most users, updating glibc is NOT necessary, but if you have a custom setuid program installed, you should update glibc to version 2.41. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-0395.

To fix the iconv vulnerability, update to Glibc-2.41 or later using the instructions from the LFS book for Glibc (sysv) or Glibc (systemd).

To update Glibc from 2.40 or earlier to 2.41 safely on a running system, some extra precautions are needed as documented in an "Important" box in the book section for Glibc. Follow it strictly or you may render the system completely unusable. YOU ARE WARNED. For LFS 12.0 and earlier, the update process will also disable and remove NSCD to get rid of the NSCD vulnerabilities.

12.2 071 BIND Date: 2025-02-01 Severity: High

In BIND-9.20.5, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service condition causing severe performance degredations and crashes. The first issue occurs due to DNS-over-HTTPS flooding, and it was resolved by adjusting named to handle HTTP/2 data in smaller chunks and throttling reading more chunks until the remote side acknowledges that it has read the response data. It also throttles clients that send far too many requests at once. The named server will also evaluate excessive streams opened by clients that include no DNS data, and will log these clients for an administrator to review them (as well as automatically blocking them from sending more requests). The second issue occurs due to a bug that could allow for many records in the additional section to cause CPU exhaustion, and it was fixed by limiting additional section processing for large RDATA sets (capping it at more than 13 names). The issues only affect the BIND server and not the utilities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-11187 and CVE-2024-12705.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to BIND-9.20.5 or later using the instructions from BIND (sysv) or BIND (systemd).

12.2 070 OpenJDK Date: 2025-01-28 Severity: Medium

In OpenJDK-23.0.2, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a remote attacker (with no privileges required) to write/delete/access information on a system running a Java application. No user interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability, but the attack complexity is high. The vulnerability exists in the Hotspot component of OpenJDK. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-21502.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to OpenJDK-23.0.2 or later using the instructions from OpenJDK (sysv) or OpenJDK (systemd).

If you want to use the pre-built binaries, update to Java-23.0.2 using the instructions from Java (sysv) or Java (systemd).

12.2 069 abseil-cpp Date: 2025-01-24 Severity: High

In abseil-cpp-20240722.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for an out-of-bounds memory access (and subsequent crash) due to an integer overflow that occurs when creating and resizing hash containers. The vulnerability is hard to exploit, but occurs because there was no upper boundary on size arguments with some methods in absl::{flat,node}_hash_{set,map}. The vulernerability is hard to exploit because container sizes are very rarely attacker controlled. Upstream has not assigned a CVE for this vulnerability, but more details can be found at the upstream commit.

To fix this vulnerability, update to abseil-cpp-20240722.1 or later using the instructions from abseil-cpp (sysv) or abseil-cpp (systemd).

12.2 068 Node.js Date: 2025-01-22 Severity: High

In Node.js-22.13.1, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that can allow for malicious use of a reinstated constructor, a denial of service via a memory leak, and tampering with requests to backend APIs. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-22150, CVE-2025-23083, and CVE-2025-23085.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Node.js-22.13.1 or later using the instructions from Node.js (sysv) or Node.js (systemd).

In addition, if you have libuv installed and wish to migrate to the 22 series of Node.js, upgrade to a newer version of libuv using the instructions from libuv (sysv) or libuv (systemd).

Alternatively, if you do not want to upgrade libuv or want to stay on the old LTS series, update to Node.js-20.18.2 using the same instructions, just with downloading the other version.

12.2 067 vim (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-01-14 Severity: Medium

In vim-9.1.1016, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a crash or arbitrary code execution when using visual mode. The issue is caused by a heap-based buffer overflow when using the :all command while visual mode is still active, because Vim does not end visual mode and will try to access beyond the end of a line in a buffer. The updated version of Vim willl correctly reset visual mode before opening other windows and buffers, and will also verify that it won't try to access a position if the position is greater than the corresponding buffer line. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2025-22134.

To fix this vulnerability, update to vim-9.1.1016 or later using the instructions from vim (sysv) or vim (systemd).

12.2 066 git Date: 2025-01-14 Severity: Low

In git-2.48.1, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for users to be mislead into typing in passwords for trusted sites, which could be sent to untrusted sites instead. This happens because Git used to print unsanitized URLs when asking for credentials, which (in submodules and recursive clones) could allow for users to be susceptible to crafted URLs. The other vulnerability occurs because Git used to pass on Carriage Returns via the credential protocol to credential helpers, some of which may use line-reading functions that interpret Carriage Returns as line endings. You should update Git if you use it to checkout repositories with submodules in them. These vulnerabiliities have been assigned CVE-2024-50349 and CVE-2024-52006.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to git-2.48.1 or later using the instructions from git (sysv) or git (systemd).

12.2 065 rsync Date: 2025-01-14 Severity: Critical

In rsync-3.4.0, six security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, information disclosure, arbitrary leaking of files on an rsync client, path traversal (allowing a server to write files to paths on a client outside of the intended destiation directory), and for privilege escalation. This update should be considered URGENT, and needs to be applied immediately to any system that has the rsync package installed, regardless of if it is a server or a client. The most severe CVE can be exploited on *any* rsync server, and the attacker only requires anonymous read access to execute arbitrary code on the machine the server is running on. The information leak happens when verifying file checksums, and allows for uninitialized stack contents to be leaked one byte at a time. The arbitrary leaking of client files vulnerability allows for any file from the client to be exfiltrated when a client is uploading files to a server, and the path traversal vulnerabilities occur when using the --safe-links or --inc-recursive options, and the privilege escalation vulnerability occurs due to a race condition that allows when handling symbolic links. There are proof of concept exploits available as well which read SSH private keys from a user's home directory on a client, and additional proof of concepts exist which allow for ~/.bashrc to be overwritten for malicious code execution. ALL users who have rsync installed need to update IMMEDIATELY. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-12084, CVE-2024-12085, CVE-2024-12086, CVE-2024-12087, CVE-2024-12088, and CVE-2024-12747.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to rsync-3.4.0 or later using the instructions from rsync (sysv) or rsync (systemd).

12.2 064 Libreoffice Date: 2025-01-08 Severity: Medium

In Libreoffice-24.8.4.2, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for unauthorized information disclosure and for arbitrary writing of files to the filesystem. The information disclosure vulnerability occurs when URLs are constructed which expand environment variables or INI file values. These could be exfiltrated to a remote server when opening a document containing these links. The issue was fixed by removing the expansion feature from document hosted URLs. The arbitrary file write vulnerability occurs because of a path traversal issue, but only files with a .ttf file extension can be written. It can be exploited by a crafted document with embedded font file path names within it. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-12426 and CVE-2024-12425.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Libreoffice-24.8.4.2 or later using the instructions from Libreoffice (sysv) or Libreoffice (systemd).

12.2 063 Thunderbird Date: 2025-01-08 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-128.6.0esr, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for potentially exploitable crashes, remote code execution, ALPN validation failures when using redirects with Alt-Svc, and for privilege escalation attacks when using WebChannel APIs (also known as a confused deputy attack). These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-0237, CVE-2025-0238, CVE-2025-0239, CVE-2025-0240, CVE-2025-0241, CVE-2025-0242, and CVE-2025-0243.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-128.6.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.2 062 Firefox Date: 2025-01-08 Severity: High

In Firefox-128.6.0esr, seven security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for potentially exploitable crashes, remote code execution, ALPN validation failures when using redirects with Alt-Svc, and for privilege escalation attacks when using WebChannel APIs (also known as a confused deputy attack). These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-0237, CVE-2025-0238, CVE-2025-0239, CVE-2025-0240, CVE-2025-0241, CVE-2025-0242, and CVE-2025-0243.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-128.6.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.2 061 Spidermonkey Date: 2025-01-08 Severity: Medium

In Spidermonkey-128.6.0esr, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a potentially explotiable crash or arbitrary code execution. These occur when parsing a JavaScript module as JSON (which could allow cross-compartment access, leading to arbitrary code execution), or when segmenting specially crafted text (leading to memory corruption). These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2025-0240 and CVE-2025-0241.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Spidermonkey-128.6.0esr or later using the instructions from Spidermonkey (sysv) or Spidermonkey (systemd).

If you update this package, you need to update Gjs to gjs-1.82.0 or later using the instructions from Gjs (sysv) or Gjs (systemd).

If you wish to stay on Spidermonkey-115, please update to Spidermonkey-115.19.0esr instead using the same instructions as used in BLFS 12.2. You do not need to update Gjs if you take this approach.

12.2 060 Seamonkey Date: 2025-01-08 Severity: Critical

In Seamonkey-2.53.20, fifteen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, unauthorized information disclosure, applications to be mistakenly opened, remotely exploitable crashes, sandbox escapes, access to PDF and JSON objects as well as video frames cross origin, permission leaks, content security policy bypasses, and cross-site scripting exposure. One of these vulnerabilities is known to be exploited in the wild. This brings Seamonkey up to date with the security issues fixed in Firefox 128.6.0/115.19.0. If you are using Seamonkey, you should update to this version immediately. Please pay special attention to the build instructions as some options and dependencies were changed. These vulnerabilities were assigned CVE-2024-8381, CVE-2024-8382, CVE-2024-8383, CVE-2024-8384, CVE-2024-9392, CVE-2024-9393, CVE-2024-9394, CVE-2024-9401, CVE-2024-9680, CVE-2024-10458, CVE-2024-10459, CVE-2024-10463, CVE-2024-11694, CVE-2025-0238, and CVE-2025-0242.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Seamonkey-2.53.20 or later using the instructions from Seamonkey (sysv) or Seamonkey (systemd).

12.2 059 cURL Date: 2025-01-03 Severity: Low

In cURL-8.11.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for cURL to leak the password for hosts to redirected hosts under certain conditions when being asked to use a .netrc file, and when also asked to follow HTTP redirects. If you do not use a .netrc file, this vulnerability does not affect you, and there is no reason to upgrade. If you do use one though, please update to cURL-8.11.1. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-11053.

To fix this vulnerability, update to cURL-8.11.1 or later using the instructions from cURL (sysv) or cURL (systemd).

12.2 058 WebKitGTK Date: 2025-01-03 Severity: High

In WebKitGTK-2.46.5, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remotely exploitable crashes and remote code execution. All four of the issues were resolved with improved checks and memory handling, and the issues are exploitable with maliciously crafted web content. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-54479, CVE-2024-54502, CVE-2024-54505, and CVE-2024-54508.

To fix this vulnerability, update to WebKitGTK-2.46.5 or later using the instructions from WebKitGTK (sysv) or WebKitGTK (systemd).

12.2 057 Thunderbird Date: 2025-01-03 Severity: Medium

In Thunderbird-128.5.2esr, a security vulnerability was fixed which could allow for client-side path traversal when using the Matrix chatroom functionality in Thunderbird's chat client. The vulnerability occurs when using malicious MXC URIs, and allows a malicious room member to issue arbirtary authenticated GET requests to the client's homeserver (in this context, that would be Thunderbird). If you use the Matrix chatroom functionality, you should update Thunderbird. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-50336.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Thunderbird-128.5.2esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.2 056 Jinja2 (LFS) Date: 2025-01-03 Severity: High

In Jinja2-3.1.5, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for sandbox escapes and execution of arbitrary Python code. One of these issues happens due to an oversight in how the Jinja sandboxed environment detects calls to str.format, and the other occurs due to a bug in the Jinja2 compiler that allows an attacker which controls both the content and filename of a template to execute arbitrary Python code outside of the sandbox. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-56201 and CVE-2024-56326.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Jinja2-3.1.5 or later using the instructions from the LFS book for Jinja2 (sysv) or Jinja2 (systemd).

12.2 055 Subversion Date: 2025-01-03 Severity: Low

In Subversion-1.14.5, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service when a revision property which contains control characters is committed to a repository. This is a repeat of CVE-2013-1968, and only affects the mod_dav_svn module (which you would use to allow access to a repository over HTTP). Local repositories, and those served by svnserve, are unaffected. The disruption can also allow for repository corruption, but it will take some time as a full dump/load cycle will be required depending on the corruption. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-46901.

To fix this vulnerability, update to Subversion-1.14.5 or later using the instructions from Subversion (sysv) or Subversion (systemd).

12.2 054 Python3 (LFS and BLFS) Date: 2025-01-03 Severity: Medium

In Python 3.13.1 (and 3.12.8), three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for unauthorized command execution when spawning a virtual environment, for filtering bypassses (because IPv4-mapped IPv6 addess properties were highly inconsistent), and for pyrepl to read local files unexpectedly (which is known to cause inconsistent behavior and arbitrary code execution). This update has caused some issues with other packages, namely Firefox and Thunderbird. If you install this security update, make sure to use the instructions from the development book for Firefox and Thunderbird (which include applying a patch to fix the build issues). Only one of these vulnerabilities has been assigned a CVE. It has been assigned CVE-2024-9287. Additional information about the other two vulnerabilities can be found at Python Issue #125140 and Python Issue #122792.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Python-3.13.1 (or 3.12.8 if you are on 3.12.x) using the instructions from Python (sysv) or Python (systemd).

12.2 053 gstreamer Date: 2024-12-04 Severity: Critical

In the 1.24.10 release of the gstreamer stack, over 40 security vulnerabilities were resolved. These issues occur in a variety of plugins, including the MP4/MOV playback support, the ID3v2 tag parser, the JPEG decoder, the WebM demuxer, the Vorbis decoder, the SSA subtitle parser, the Opus decoder, the gdk-pixbuf decoder, the WAV parser, the AVI subtitle parser, and the LRC subtitle parser, as well as in the gst-discoverer-1.0 utility. Because of the amount of these vulnerabilities as well as the plugins that they impact, you should update the gstreamer stack immediately if you have it installed. All of these issues can allow for crashes, but many of them also allow for arbitrary code execution, or remote code execution (in the context of using a web browser playing WebM/MP4/MOV videos or WAV sounds on web pages). Most of these vulnerabilities have CVEs, but all of them have additional information from the GitHub Security Lab. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-47537, CVE-2024-47598, CVE-2024-47539, CVE-2024-47542, CVE-2024-47543, CVE-2024-47545, CVE-2024-47544, CVE-2024-47597, CVE-2024-47546, CVE-2024-47606, CVE-2024-47596, CVE-2024-47599, CVE-2024-47540, CVE-2024-47600, CVE-2024-47602, CVE-2024-47601, CVE-2024-47603, CVE-2024-47538, CVE-2024-47541, CVE-2024-47607, CVE-2024-47613, CVE-2024-47615, CVE-2024-47778, CVE-2024-47777, CVE-2024-47776, CVE-2024-47775, CVE-2024-47774, CVE-2024-47835, and CVE-2024-47834.

Additional information about these vulnerabilities can be found at Gstreamer Security Advisories.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update the entire gstreamer stack to 1.24.10 by building through the packages starting with gstreamer (sysv) or gstreamer (systemd).

12.2 052 QtWebEngine Date: 2024-12-04 Severity: Critical

In QtWebEngine-6.8.1, seventeen security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution, unauthorized access to data, UI spoofing, and remotely exploitable crashes. These vulnerabilities are in a variety of subsystems in Chromium, including Mojo, Dawn, V8, Extensions, DevTools, Navigation, Web Authentication, Paint, FileSystem, Blink, Media, Views, and Serial; and all of them are exploitable via maliciously crafted web pages (and in some cases, malicious advertisements on web pages). These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-9369, CVE-2024-10487, CVE-2024-10230, CVE-2024-10231, CVE-2024-10229, CVE-2024-9965, CVE-2024-9966, CVE-2024-9959, CVE-2024-9955, CVE-2024-9602, CVE-2024-9603, CVE-2024-11116, CVE-2024-11117, CVE-2024-11110, CVE-2024-11112, CVE-2024-11114, and CVE-2024-10827.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to QtWebEngine-6.8.1 or later using the instructions from QtWebEngine (sysv) or QtWebEngine (systemd).

12.2 051 WebKitGTK Date: 2024-11-29 Severity: Critical

In WebKitGTK-2.46.4, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution and cross site scripting attacks. These issues can occur when processing maliciously crafted web content, and there are numerous reports of the issues being exploited in the wild. They were fixed with improved checks and improved state management. If you have WebKitGTK installed, you need to update to 2.46.4 or later immediately. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-44308 and CVE-2024-44309.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to WebKitGTK-2.46.4 or later using the instructions from WebKitGTK (sysv) or WebKitGTK (systemd).

12.2 050 libjxl Date: 2024-11-29 Severity: High

In libjxl-0.11.1, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for arbitrary code execution or a denial of service condition (stack exhaustion leading to an out-of-memory condition). Both of these issues can be exploited by opening/loading a malicious JXL image, but the arbitrary code execution problem can occur when calling JxlEncoderAddJPEGFrame to encode a frame into a JXL file. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-11403 and CVE-2024-11498.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libjxl-0.11.1 or later using the instructions from libjxl (sysv) or libjxl (systemd).

12.2 049 Thunderbird Date: 2024-11-26 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-128.5.0esr, six security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for select list elements to be shown over another site (leading to website spoofing), content security policy bypasses, cross-site scripting, URL bar spoofing, remotely exploitable crashes, improper keypress handling when executing files, and for remote code execution. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-11692, CVE-2024-11694, CVE-2024-11695, CVE-2024-11696, CVE_2024-11697, and CVE-2024-11699.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-128.5.0esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.2 048 Firefox Date: 2024-11-26 Severity: High

In Firefox-128.5.0esr, six security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for select list elements to be shown over another site (leading to website spoofing), content security policy bypasses, cross-site scripting, URL bar spoofing, remotely exploitable crashes, improper keypress handling when executing files, and for remote code execution. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-11692, CVE-2024-11694, CVE-2024-11695, CVE-2024-11696, CVE_2024-11697, and CVE-2024-11699.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Firefox-128.5.0esr or later using the instructions from Firefox (sysv) or Firefox (systemd).

12.2 047 libsoup3 Date: 2024-11-25 Severity: High

In libsoup-3.6.1, three security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for HTTP Request Smuggling, arbitrary code execution, and remotely exploitable crashes (and out-of-memory conditions). The HTTP Request Smuggling vulnerability occurs because '\0' characters at the end of header names are ignored in some configurations. The arbitrary code execution vulnerability occurs in applications that perform conversion to UTF-8 in soup_header_parse_param_list_strict due to a buffer overflow, but note that input received over the network cannot trigger this (and thus the issue is not exploitable remotely). The remotely exploitable crashes (and out-of-memory conditions) are caused by an infinite loop during the reading of certain patterns of WebSocket data from clients. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-52530, CVE-2024-52531, and CVE-2024-52532.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to libsoup-3.6.1 or later using the instructions from libsoup (sysv) or libsoup (systemd).

12.2 046 Wireshark Date: 2024-11-25 Severity: Medium

In Wireshark-4.4.2, two security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for a denial of service condition (application crash and out-of-memory condition) when dissecting FiveCo RAP and ECMP packets. These issues can be exploited by crafted PCAP files, but users do not need to update if they are not capturing packets that use either of those protocols. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-11595 and CVE-2024-11596.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Wireshark-4.4.2 or later using the instructions from Wireshark (sysv) or Wireshark (systemd).

12.2 045 PHP Date: 2024-11-25 Severity: Critical

In PHP-8.4.1 (or 8.3.14), five security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for remote code execution (when using the CLI interface to SAPI), remote code execution when using LDAP on a 32-bit system, unauthorized disclosure of MySQL query responses, remote code execution when using the Firebird and dblib quoters, CRLF injection when configuring a proxy in a stream context (leading to HTTP request smuggling attacks), and for remotely exploitable crashes when using the convert.quoted-printable-decode filter in a program. Proof of concept exploits for these vulnerabilities were made public with the release of the new versions of PHP. The vulnerabilities are in a variety of subsystems, including Streams, PDO DBLIB, PDO Firebird, MySQLnd, LDAP, and the CLI, and the BLFS team thus recommends updating PHP on any system that is used as a server. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-8932, CVE-2024-8929, CVE-2024-11236, CVE-2024-11234, and CVE-2024-11233.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to PHP-8.4.1 (or 8.3.14) or later using the instructions from PHP (sysv) or PHP (systemd).

12.2 044 PostgreSQL Date: 2024-11-25 Severity: High

In PostgreSQL-17.1, four security vulnerabilities were fixed that could allow for users to complete unauthoried reads and modifications, for man-in-the-middle attackers to send fabricated error messages, for SET ROLE and SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION to be set to wrong user IDs, and for an unprivileged database user to change sensitive process environment variables to achieve arbitrary code execution. A proof of concept exploit exists for the arbitrary code execution vulnerability, but note that it requires use of the PostgreSQL PL/Perl functionality. The PostgreSQL-17.1 update introduced some regressions relating to these security fixes that required a follow-up release, and the BLFS team recommends using PostgreSQL-17.2 as a result. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE-2024-10976, CVE-2024-10977, CVE-2024-10978, and CVE-2024-10979.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to PostgreSQL-17.2 or later using the instructions from PostgreSQL (sysv) or PostgreSQL (systemd).

12.2 043 glib Date: 2024-11-25 Severity: Critical

In glib-2.82.1, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a buffer overflow in the SOCKS4 proxy support within glib. The issue occurs due to an off-by-one error and then buffer overflow because SOCKS4_CONN_MSG_LEN in gio/gsocks4aproxy.c is not sufficient for a trailing '\0' character that set_connect_msg() appends after a hostname. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-52533.

To fix this vulnerability, update to glib-2.82.1 or later using the instructions from glib (sysv) or glib (systemd).

12.2 042 Thunderbird Date: 2024-11-15 Severity: High

In Thunderbird-128.4.3esr, one security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for messages encrypted with OpenPGP to be sent in plain text. This vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2024-11159.

To fix these vulnerabilities, update to Thunderbird-128.4.3esr or later using the instructions from Thunderbird (sysv) or Thunderbird (systemd).

12.2 041 Expat (LFS) Date: 2024-11-10 Severity: Medium

In Expat-2.6.4, a security vulnerability was fixed that could allow for a denial of service condition (application crash) when using the XML_ResumeParser function due to a NULL pointer dereference.
